title.en: Volume 37 Biographies 27: Shen Qingzhi, Zong Que
title.raw: 卷三十七 列傳第二十七 沈慶之 宗愨 Volume 37 Biographies 27: Shen Qingzhi, Zong Que

sentences.zh: 列傳第二十七

translations.literal: Biographies 27
translations.idiomatic: Biographies, Number Twenty-Seven

sentences.zh: 沈慶之宗愨

translations.literal: Shen Qingzhi, Zong Que
translations.idiomatic: Shen Qingzhi · Zong Que

sentences.zh: 永初二年，慶之除殿中員外將軍，又隨伯符隸到彥之北侵。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongchu, Qingzhi was appointed Supernumerary General of the Palace Attendants, and also followed Bofu in serving under Dao Yanzhi on the northern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongchu, Qingzhi was made Supernumerary General of the Palace Attendants and joined Bofu in serving under Dao Yanzhi on the northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 伯符病歸，仍隸檀道濟。

translations.literal: When Bofu fell ill and returned home, Qingzhi was transferred to Tan Daoji's command.
translations.idiomatic: After Bofu fell ill and returned home, he was assigned to Tan Daoji's command.

sentences.zh: 道濟白文帝稱慶之忠謹曉兵，上使領隊防東掖門，稍得引接，出入禁省。

translations.literal: Daoji reported to Emperor Wen that Qingzhi was loyal, careful, and knowledgeable in military affairs; the emperor had him lead a guard detail at the Eastern Side Gate, gradually granting him audience and access to the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji recommended Qingzhi to Emperor Wen as loyal, diligent, and well versed in military affairs. The emperor put him in charge of a guard unit at the Eastern Side Gate and gradually brought him into the inner circle, allowing him to enter and leave the forbidden palace precincts.

sentences.zh: 領軍劉湛知之，欲相引接，謂曰：「卿在省年月久遠，比當相論。

translations.literal: The Director of Palace Attendants Liu Zhan learned of this and wished to bring him into his circle, saying: "You have been in the palace for many years; I ought to speak on your behalf soon."
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Palace Attendants Liu Zhan learned of this and sought to patronize him, saying, "You have been in the palace service for many years — it is high time I spoke on your behalf."

sentences.zh: 」慶之正色曰：「下官在省十年，自應得轉，不復以此仰累。

translations.literal: Qingzhi replied sternly: "I have been in the palace for ten years and ought to be promoted on my own merits; I will not impose upon you for that."
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi answered with a stern face: "Your humble servant has been in the palace for ten years and ought to earn promotion on his own merits. I will not burden you with such a request."

sentences.zh: 」尋轉正員將軍。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was promoted to Regular General.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to full Regular General.

sentences.zh: 及湛被收之夕，上開門召慶之，慶之戎服履襪縛褲入，上見而驚曰：「卿何意乃爾急裝？

translations.literal: On the night when Zhan was arrested, the emperor opened the gate and summoned Qingzhi; Qingzhi entered in military garb, boots, and trousers tied at the ankles. The emperor was startled and said: "Why are you dressed so urgently?"
translations.idiomatic: On the night Zhan was arrested, the emperor opened the gate and summoned Qingzhi. Qingzhi entered in full military dress — armor, boots, and trousers bound at the ankles. The emperor was startled and said, "Why have you dressed in such haste?"

sentences.zh: 」慶之曰：「夜半喚隊主，不容緩服。

translations.literal: Qingzhi said: "When the squad commander is summoned at midnight, one cannot dress at leisure."
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi replied, "When a squad commander is summoned at midnight, he cannot afford to dress at his ease."

sentences.zh: 」遣收吳郡太守劉斌殺之。

translations.literal: The emperor sent to arrest Liu Bin, Administrator of Wu Commandery, and had him executed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent to arrest Liu Bin, Administrator of Wu Commandery, and had him put to death.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十九年，雍州刺史劉道產卒，群蠻大動，征西司馬朱修之討蠻失利，以慶之為建威將軍，率眾助修之。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Yuanjia, when Liu Daochan, Inspector of Yong Province, died, the barbarian tribes rose up on a large scale. Zhu Xiuzhi, Western Campaigning Marshal, suffered defeat in suppressing them. Qingzhi was appointed General Who Establishes Might and led troops to assist Xiuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Yuanjia, when Liu Daochan, Inspector of Yong Province, died, the tribal peoples rose in great numbers. Zhu Xiuzhi, Western Campaigning Marshal, was defeated in his campaign against them. Qingzhi was appointed General Who Establishes Might and led troops to assist Xiuzhi.

sentences.zh: 修之失律下獄，慶之專軍進討，大破緣沔諸蠻。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi was imprisoned for military misconduct; Qingzhi took sole command and advanced in attack, crushing the barbarian tribes along the Han River.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi was imprisoned for military failure. Qingzhi took sole command and pressed the attack, crushing the tribal forces all along the Han River.

sentences.zh: 後為孝武撫軍中兵參軍。

translations.literal: Later he served as Middle Army Adjutant on the staff of Emperor Xiaowu's Pacifying Army.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Middle Army Adjutant on the staff of Emperor Xiaowu's Pacifying Army.

sentences.zh: 孝武以本號為雍州，隨府西上，征蠻寇屢有功。

translations.literal: When Xiaowu was given Yong Province under his former title, Qingzhi accompanied the headquarters west and repeatedly distinguished himself in campaigns against barbarian raiders.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowu was assigned Yong Province under his former title, Qingzhi accompanied the headquarters westward and repeatedly distinguished himself in campaigns against tribal raiders.

sentences.zh: 還都，復為廣陵王誕北中郎中兵參軍，加建威將軍、南濟陰太守。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, he again served as Middle Army Adjutant in the Northern Central Office of Prince Dan of Guangling, with the additional titles of General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Southern Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to the capital, he again served as Middle Army Adjutant in the Northern Central Office of Prince Dan of Guangling, with the additional titles of General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Southern Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 雍州蠻又為寇，慶之以將軍、太守復與隨王誕入沔。

translations.literal: When the barbarians of Yong Province raided again, Qingzhi, in his capacity as general and administrator, once more entered the Han River region with Prince Dan of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: When the tribes of Yong Province raided again, Qingzhi, in his capacity as general and administrator, once more entered the Han River region with Prince Dan of Sui.

sentences.zh: 及至襄陽，率後軍中兵參軍柳元景、隨郡太守宗愨等伐沔北諸山蠻，大破之。

translations.literal: Upon reaching Xiangyang, he led Rear Army Middle Adjutant Liu Yuanjing, Administrator of Sui Commandery Zong Que, and others to attack the mountain barbarians north of the Han, crushing them decisively.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching Xiangyang, he led Rear Army Middle Adjutant Liu Yuanjing, Administrator of Sui Commandery Zong Que, and others against the mountain tribes north of the Han, crushing them decisively.

sentences.zh: 威震諸山，群蠻皆稽顙。

translations.literal: His renown shook the mountains; the barbarian tribes all prostrated themselves in submission.
translations.idiomatic: His renown shook every mountain; the tribal peoples all prostrated themselves in submission.

sentences.zh: 慶之患頭風，好著狐皮帽，群蠻惡之，號曰蒼頭公。

translations.literal: Qingzhi suffered from headaches and liked to wear a fox-fur cap; the barbarians abhorred this and called him the Grey-headed Lord.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi suffered from headaches and liked to wear a fox-fur cap. The tribes detested the sight and called him the Grey-headed Lord.

sentences.zh: 每見慶之軍，輒畏懼曰：「蒼頭公已復來矣。」

translations.literal: Whenever they saw Qingzhi's army, they would cry out in fear: "The Grey-headed Lord has come again!"
translations.idiomatic: Whenever they saw Qingzhi's army, they cried out in terror: "The Grey-headed Lord has come again!"

sentences.zh: 慶之引軍出，前後破降甚眾，又討犬羊諸山蠻，緣險築重城，施門櫓甚峻。

translations.literal: Qingzhi led his army forth; before and after he defeated and received the surrender of vast numbers. He also attacked the mountain barbarians of Quanyang, who built fortified cities along perilous terrain with imposing gate-towers and watchturrets.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi led his army forth and, in campaign after campaign, defeated and received the surrender of vast numbers. He also attacked the mountain tribes of Quanyang, who had built fortified strongholds along perilous heights with imposing gate-towers and watchturrets.

sentences.zh: 慶之連營山下，營中開門相通。

translations.literal: Qingzhi encamped his forces in linked camps at the foot of the mountains; the camps had gates opening into one another.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi encamped his forces in linked camps at the foot of the mountains, with gates between the camps opening into one another.

sentences.zh: 又令諸軍各穿池于營內，朝夕不外汲。

translations.literal: He also ordered each unit to dig pools within its camp so they need not go outside for water morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered each unit to dig pools within its camp so that troops need not leave camp for water morning or evening.

sentences.zh: 兼以防蠻之火。

translations.literal: This also served to guard against barbarian fire attacks.
translations.idiomatic: This also served as a defense against tribal fire attacks.

sentences.zh: 頃之風甚，蠻夜下山，人提一炬燒營。

translations.literal: Before long a strong wind arose; at night the barbarians came down the mountains, each carrying a torch to burn the camps.
translations.idiomatic: Before long a strong wind arose. At night the tribes came down the mountains, each man carrying a torch to set the camps ablaze.

sentences.zh: 火至，輒以池水灌滅之。

translations.literal: When fire reached them, they doused it with the pool water.
translations.idiomatic: When the flames reached them, they doused the fire with the pool water.

sentences.zh: 蠻被圍守日久，並饑乏，自後稍出歸降。

translations.literal: The barbarians, besieged for a long time, all grew hungry and exhausted; afterward they gradually came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Besieged for a long time, the tribes grew hungry and exhausted; afterward they gradually came out to surrender.

sentences.zh: 慶之前後所獲蠻，並移都下，以為營戶。

translations.literal: All the barbarians Qingzhi captured before and after were relocated to the capital to serve as military households.
translations.idiomatic: All the tribes Qingzhi captured, in campaign after campaign, were relocated to the capital to serve as military households.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，遷太子步兵校尉。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, he was transferred to Infantry Commandant of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: During the twenty-seventh year, he was transferred to Infantry Commandant of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 其年，文帝將北侵，慶之諫曰：「道濟再行無功，彥之失利而反，今料王玄謨等未踰兩將，恐重辱王師。

translations.literal: That year, as Emperor Wen planned a northern invasion, Qingzhi remonstrated: "Daoji went twice without success; Yanzhi returned after defeat. I estimate that Wang Xuamo and the others will not surpass those two generals — I fear our armies will suffer disgrace again."
translations.idiomatic: That year, as Emperor Wen planned a northern invasion, Qingzhi remonstrated: "Daoji campaigned twice without success; Yanzhi returned in defeat. I expect that Wang Xuamo and the others will not surpass those two generals — I fear our armies will suffer disgrace once again."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「王師再屈，別有所由。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Our armies were twice humbled for other reasons.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Our armies were twice humbled for other reasons.

sentences.zh: 道濟養寇自資，彥之中塗疾動。

translations.literal: Daoji nurtured the enemy to enrich himself; Yanzhi fell ill midway.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji nurtured the enemy to enrich himself; Yanzhi fell ill midway through the campaign.

sentences.zh: 虜所恃唯馬，夏水浩大，泛舟濟河，碻磝必走，滑台小戍，易可覆拔。

translations.literal: The barbarians rely solely on their horses. In summer the rivers swell greatly; crossing the Yellow River by boat, the enemy at Quebi will surely flee. The small garrison at Huatai can easily be overrun and taken.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy relies solely on their horses. In summer the rivers swell greatly; crossing the Yellow River by boat, the force at Quebi will surely flee. The small garrison at Huatai can easily be overrun and taken.

sentences.zh: 克此二戍，館穀吊人，虎牢洛陽，自然不固。

translations.literal: Once these two strongpoints are taken and grain stored and people comforted, Hulao and Luoyang will naturally not hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: Once these two strongpoints are taken, with grain stored and the people comforted, Hulao and Luoyang will naturally not hold firm.

sentences.zh: 」慶之固陳不可，時丹陽尹徐湛之、吏部尚書江湛並在坐，上使湛之等難慶之。

translations.literal: Qingzhi firmly argued it could not be done. At the time Xu Zhanzhi, Governor of Danyang, and Jiang Zhan, Minister of Personnel, were both present; the emperor had them debate Qingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi firmly argued that it could not be done. Xu Zhanzhi, Governor of Danyang, and Jiang Zhan, Minister of Personnel, were both present; the emperor had them debate Qingzhi.

sentences.zh: 慶之曰：「為國譬如家，耕當問奴，織當訪婢。

translations.literal: Qingzhi said: "Governing a state is like managing a household — for plowing one should ask the farmhand, for weaving one should consult the maid."
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi said, "Governing a state is like managing a household — for plowing one should ask the farmhand, for weaving one should consult the maid."

sentences.zh: 陛下今欲伐國，而與白面書生輩謀之，事何由濟？

translations.literal: Your Majesty now wishes to invade a foreign state yet plans it with pale-faced bookish fellows — how can the enterprise succeed?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty now wishes to invade a foreign state, yet you plan it with pale-faced bookish fellows — how can the enterprise succeed?

sentences.zh: 「上大笑。

translations.literal: The emperor laughed heartily.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then laughed heartily.

sentences.zh: 及軍行，慶之副玄謨。

translations.literal: When the army marched, Qingzhi served as deputy to Xuamo.
translations.idiomatic: Once the army marched, Qingzhi served as deputy to Xuamo.

sentences.zh: 玄謨進圍滑台，慶之與蕭斌留守碻磝，仍領斌輔國司馬。

translations.literal: Xuamo advanced to besiege Huatai; Qingzhi and Xiao Bin remained to hold Quebi, and Qingzhi also served as Bin's Pacifying Army Major.
translations.idiomatic: Xuamo advanced to besiege Huatai. Qingzhi and Xiao Bin remained to hold Quebi, and Qingzhi also served as Bin's Pacifying Army Major.

sentences.zh: 玄謨攻滑台，積旬不拔，魏太武大軍南向，斌遣慶之將五千人救玄謨。

translations.literal: Xuamo assaulted Huatai for many days without taking it. The Wei Emperor Taiwu led his great army southward; Bin sent Qingzhi with five thousand men to rescue Xuamo.
translations.idiomatic: Xuamo assaulted Huatai for many days without taking it. The Wei Emperor Taiwu led his great army southward, and Bin sent Qingzhi with five thousand men to rescue Xuamo.

sentences.zh: 慶之曰：「少軍輕往，必無益也。

translations.literal: Qingzhi said: "Sending a small force lightly will surely do no good."
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi said, "Sending a small force lightly will surely do no good."

sentences.zh: 」會玄謨退還，斌將斬之，慶之諫乃止。

translations.literal: Just then Xuamo retreated; Bin was about to execute him, but Qingzhi remonstrated and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Xuamo retreated. Bin was about to execute him, but Qingzhi remonstrated and stopped it.

sentences.zh: 蕭斌以前驅敗績，欲死固碻磝，慶之以為不可。

translations.literal: Xiao Bin, because the vanguard had been defeated, wished to die defending Quebi; Qingzhi thought this unwise.
translations.idiomatic: Because the vanguard had been defeated, Xiao Bin wished to die defending Quebi; Qingzhi thought this unwise.

sentences.zh: 會制使至，不許退，諸將並宜留。

translations.literal: Then an imperial messenger arrived ordering no retreat — all generals should remain.
translations.idiomatic: Then an imperial messenger arrived ordering no retreat — all generals were to remain.

sentences.zh: 斌復問計于慶之，慶之曰：「閫外之事，將所得專，制從遠來，事勢已異。

translations.literal: Bin asked Qingzhi's advice again; Qingzhi said: "Matters outside the gate are for the general's sole discretion; orders come from afar, but circumstances have already changed."
translations.idiomatic: Bin asked Qingzhi's advice again. Qingzhi said, "Matters outside the gate are for the general's sole discretion. Orders come from afar, but circumstances have already changed."

sentences.zh: 節下有一范增而不能用，空議何施？

translations.literal: You have a Fan Zeng at your side yet cannot use him — of what use are empty deliberations?
translations.idiomatic: You have a Fan Zeng at your side yet cannot use him — of what use are empty deliberations?"

sentences.zh: 」斌及坐者並笑曰：「沈公乃更學問。

translations.literal: Bin and all present laughed: "Master Shen has become quite the scholar."
translations.idiomatic: Bin and all present laughed and said, "Master Shen has become quite the scholar."

sentences.zh: 」慶之厲聲曰：「眾人雖見古今，不如下官耳學也。

translations.literal: Qingzhi said loudly: "Though you all may have read of past and present, you are not the equal of what I have heard."
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi said loudly, "Though you all may have read of past and present, you are not the equal of what I have heard with my own ears."

sentences.zh: 」玄謨自以退敗，求戍碻磝。

translations.literal: Xuamo, considering himself disgraced by retreat, asked to garrison Quebi.
translations.idiomatic: Xuamo, considering himself disgraced by retreat, asked to garrison Quebi.

sentences.zh: 斌乃還曆城。

translations.literal: Bin then returned to Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: Bin thereupon returned to Licheng.

sentences.zh: 申坦、垣護之共據清口，慶之奔驛馳歸。

translations.literal: Shen Tan and Yuan Huzhi jointly held Qingkou; Qingzhi raced back by post relay.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Tan and Yuan Huzhi jointly held Qingkou. Qingzhi raced back by post relay.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，師復行，慶之固諫不從。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, the army marched again; Qingzhi remonstrated firmly but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year, the army marched again. Qingzhi remonstrated firmly but was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 以立議不同，不使北出。

translations.literal: Because his counsel differed, he was not allowed to go north.
translations.idiomatic: Because his counsel differed, the court did not allow him to go north.

sentences.zh: 是時亡命司馬黑石、廬江叛吏夏侯方進在西陽五水讙動群蠻，自淮汝間至江沔，咸離其患，乃遣慶之督諸將討之，制江、豫、荊、雍並遣軍受慶之節度。

translations.literal: At that time the fugitive Sima Heishi and the rebel official of Lujiang Xiahou Fangjin stirred up the tribal peoples in the five rivers of Xiyang; from between the Huai and Ru rivers to the Yangtze and Han, all suffered their depredations. The court dispatched Qingzhi to command the generals in suppressing them, and Jiang, Yu, Jing, and Yong provinces were all ordered to send troops under Qingzhi's command.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the fugitive Sima Heishi and the rebel official of Lujiang Xiahou Fangjin stirred up the tribal peoples in the five rivers of Xiyang; from between the Huai and Ru rivers to the Yangtze and Han, all suffered their depredations. The court dispatched Qingzhi to command the generals in suppressing them, and Jiang, Yu, Jing, and Yong provinces were all ordered to send troops under his command.

sentences.zh: 三十年，孝武出次五洲，總統群帥。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, Xiaowu encamped at Wuzhou to command all the generals.
translations.idiomatic: During the thirtieth year, Xiaowu encamped at Wuzhou to command all the generals.

sentences.zh: 慶之從巴水出至五洲諮受軍略。

translations.literal: Qingzhi came out from the Ba River to Wuzhou to receive military instructions.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi then came out from the Ba River to Wuzhou to receive military instructions.

sentences.zh: 會孝武典簽董元嗣自建鄴還，陳元凶弑逆，孝武遣慶之引諸軍。

translations.literal: When Xiaowu's chief clerk Dong Yuansi returned from Jiankang and reported the crown prince's regicide, Xiaowu dispatched Qingzhi to lead all armies.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowu's chief clerk Dong Yuansi returned from Jiankang and reported the crown prince's regicide, Xiaowu dispatched Qingzhi to lead all the armies.

sentences.zh: 慶之謂腹心曰：「蕭斌婦人不足數，其餘將帥並易與耳。

translations.literal: Qingzhi told his inner circle: "Xiao Bin is not worth mentioning; the rest of the commanders are all easy opponents."
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi told his trusted confidants, "Xiao Bin is not worth mentioning, and the rest of the commanders are all easy opponents."

sentences.zh: 今輔順討逆，不憂不濟也。

translations.literal: Now aiding the righteous and punishing the rebel — I have no worry of failure.
translations.idiomatic: Now that we aid the righteous and punish the rebel, I have no worry of failure."

sentences.zh: 」時元凶密與慶之書，令殺孝武。

translations.literal: At that time the villain secretly sent Qingzhi a letter ordering him to kill Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: By then the villain secretly sent Qingzhi a letter ordering him to kill Xiaowu.

sentences.zh: 慶之入求見，孝武稱疾不敢見。

translations.literal: Qingzhi entered requesting audience; Xiaowu pleaded illness and dared not see him.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi then entered requesting audience; Xiaowu pleaded illness and dared not see him.

sentences.zh: 慶之突前，以元凶手書呈簡，孝武泣求入內與母辭。

translations.literal: Qingzhi pressed forward and presented the villain's letter on a bamboo slip; Xiaowu wept and begged to go inside to bid farewell to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi pressed forward and presented the villain's letter on a bamboo slip. Xiaowu wept and begged to go inside to bid farewell to his mother.

sentences.zh: 慶之曰：「下官受先帝厚恩，常願報德，今日之事，唯力是視，殿下是何疑之深。

translations.literal: Qingzhi said: "I have received great favor from the late emperor and have long wished to repay it; in today's matter I will give all my strength — why does Your Highness doubt so deeply?"
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi said, "Your humble servant has received great favor from the late emperor and has long wished to repay it. In today's matter I will give all my strength — why does Your Highness doubt so deeply?"

sentences.zh: 」帝起再拜曰：「家國安危，在於將軍。

translations.literal: The emperor rose and bowed twice: "The safety of house and state rests on the general."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rose and bowed twice, saying, "The safety of house and state rests on the general."

sentences.zh: 」慶之即勒內外處分。

translations.literal: Qingzhi immediately organized disposition of forces inside and out.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi immediately organized the disposition of forces inside and out.

sentences.zh: 府主簿顏竣聞慶之至，馳入見帝曰：「今四方尚未知義師之舉，而劭據有天府，首尾不相應赴，此危道也。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Yan Jun, hearing Qingzhi had arrived, raced in to see the emperor: "The four quarters do not yet know the righteous army has risen, while Liu Shao holds the imperial capital; head and tail cannot respond to each other — this is a perilous course."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Yan Jun, hearing Qingzhi had arrived, raced in to see the emperor and said, "The four quarters do not yet know the righteous army has risen, while Liu Shao holds the imperial capital. Head and tail cannot respond to each other — this is a perilous course."

sentences.zh: 宜待諸鎮唇齒，然後舉事。

translations.literal: We should wait for the provinces to stand together like lips and teeth, then act.
translations.idiomatic: We should wait for the provinces to stand together like lips and teeth, and only then act."

sentences.zh: 」慶之厲聲曰：「今方興大事，而黃頭小兒皆參預，此禍至矣，宜斬以徇眾。

translations.literal: Qingzhi said loudly: "We are embarking on a great enterprise, yet yellow-headed striplings all join in deliberation — disaster approaches; he should be executed as a warning to all."
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi said loudly, "We are embarking on a great enterprise, yet yellow-headed striplings all join in deliberation — disaster approaches. He should be executed as a warning to all."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「竣何不拜謝。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Jun, why not bow in thanks?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Jun, why not bow in thanks?"

sentences.zh: 」竣起再拜。

translations.literal: Jun rose and bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: Jun rose and bowed twice in thanks.

sentences.zh: 慶之曰：「君但當知筆劄之事。

translations.literal: Qingzhi said: "You need only know matters of brush and document."
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi said, "You need only know matters of brush and document."

sentences.zh: 」於是處分，旬日內外整辦，時皆謂神兵。

translations.literal: Thereupon he made disposition; within ten days inside and out were fully prepared, and all called them divine troops.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he made his disposition; within ten days inside and out were fully prepared, and all called them divine troops.

sentences.zh: 百姓欣悅。

translations.literal: The common people rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: The people rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 眾軍既集，假慶之為武昌內史，領府司馬。

translations.literal: Once all armies were gathered, Qingzhi was given provisional appointment as Internal Administrator of Wuchang and chief major of the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Once all armies were gathered, Qingzhi was given provisional appointment as Internal Administrator of Wuchang and chief major of the headquarters.

sentences.zh: 孝武至尋陽，慶之及柳元景等並勸即大位，不許。

translations.literal: When Xiaowu reached Xunyang, Qingzhi and Liu Yuanjing and others all urged immediate accession to the throne; he did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowu reached Xunyang, Qingzhi and Liu Yuanjing and others all urged him to ascend the throne immediately; he did not consent.

sentences.zh: 賊劭遣慶之門生錢無忌齎書說慶之解甲，慶之執無忌白之。

translations.literal: The rebel Liu Shao sent Qingzhi's former student Qian Wuji with a letter trying to persuade Qingzhi to lay down arms; Qingzhi seized Wuji and reported him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Liu Shao sent Qingzhi's former student Qian Wuji with a letter trying to persuade Qingzhi to lay down arms. Qingzhi seized Wuji and reported him.

sentences.zh: 孝武踐阼，以慶之為領軍將軍，尋出為南兗州刺史，加都督，鎮盱眙，封南昌縣公。

translations.literal: When Xiaowu ascended the throne, Qingzhi was made General of the Palace Attendants; soon after he went out as Inspector of Southern Yan Province with grand command, garrisoning Xuyi, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Nanchang county.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowu ascended the throne, Qingzhi was made General of the Palace Attendants. Soon after he went out as Inspector of Southern Yan Province with grand command, garrisoning Xuyi, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Nanchang county.

sentences.zh: 大明三年，司空竟陵王誕據廣陵反，復以慶之為車騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，固讓南兗州刺史，加都督，率眾討之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daming, Minister of Works Prince Dan of Jingling rebelled holding Guangling; Qingzhi was again appointed Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry with privilege equal to the Three Dukes, firmly declining the post of Inspector of Southern Yan while retaining grand command, leading troops to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Daming, Minister of Works Prince Dan of Jingling rebelled holding Guangling. Qingzhi was again appointed Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry with privilege equal to the Three Dukes, firmly declining the post of Inspector of Southern Yan while retaining grand command, and led troops to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 誕遣客沈道湣齎書說慶之，餉以玉環刀。

translations.literal: Dan sent his retainer Shen Daomin with a letter to persuade Qingzhi, presenting a jade-ring knife as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: Dan sent his retainer Shen Daomin with a letter to persuade Qingzhi, presenting a jade-ring knife as a gift.

sentences.zh: 慶之遣道湣反，數以罪惡。

translations.literal: Qingzhi sent Daomin back, listing their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi sent Daomin back, enumerating their crimes.

sentences.zh: 慶之至城下，誕登樓謂曰：「沈公，君白首之年，何為來此？

translations.literal: When Qingzhi reached the foot of the walls, Dan mounted the tower and said: "Master Shen, in your white-haired years — why have you come here?"
translations.idiomatic: When Qingzhi reached the foot of the walls, Dan mounted the tower and said, "Master Shen, in your white-haired years — why have you come here?"

sentences.zh: 」慶之曰：「朝廷以君狂愚，不足勞少壯，故使僕來耳。

translations.literal: Qingzhi said: "The court considers you mad and foolish — not worth troubling the young and strong — so they sent me."
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi said, "The court considers you mad and foolish — not worth troubling the young and strong — so they sent me."

sentences.zh: 」慶之塞塹，造攻道，立行樓土山並諸攻具。

translations.literal: Qingzhi filled the moat, built assault ramps, erected mobile towers and earthen mounds, and all manner of siege equipment.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi filled the moat, built assault ramps, and erected mobile towers, earthen mounds, and all manner of siege equipment.

sentences.zh: 時夏雨不得攻城，上使御史中丞庾徽之奏免慶之官以激之，制無所問。

translations.literal: Summer rains at the time prevented assault; the emperor had Censor-in-Chief Yu Huizhi memorialize to dismiss Qingzhi from office to spur him on; the imperial rescript took no notice of the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Summer rains at the time prevented assault. The emperor had Censor-in-Chief Yu Huizhi memorialize to dismiss Qingzhi from office to spur him on; the imperial rescript took no notice of the memorial.

sentences.zh: 誕餉慶之食，提挈者百餘人，慶之不開，悉焚之。

translations.literal: Dan sent food to Qingzhi, carried by more than a hundred attendants; Qingzhi did not open the gate and burned it all.
translations.idiomatic: Dan sent food to Qingzhi, carried by more than a hundred attendants. Qingzhi did not open the gate and burned it all.

sentences.zh: 誕於城上投函表，令慶之為送。

translations.literal: Dan cast down sealed memorials from the walls, asking Qingzhi to deliver them.
translations.idiomatic: Dan cast down sealed memorials from the walls, asking Qingzhi to deliver them.

sentences.zh: 慶之曰：「我奉制討賊，不得為汝送表。

translations.literal: Qingzhi said: "I bear orders to punish the rebel and cannot deliver your memorials for you."
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi said, "I bear orders to punish the rebel and cannot deliver your memorials for you."

sentences.zh: 」每攻城，慶之輒身先士卒。

translations.literal: Every time they assaulted the walls, Qingzhi personally led the charge ahead of his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Each time they assaulted the walls, Qingzhi personally led the charge ahead of his troops.

sentences.zh: 上戒之曰：「卿為統任，當令處分有方，何須身受矢石邪？

translations.literal: The emperor admonished him: "As supreme commander you should direct affairs with method — why must you personally face arrows and stones?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admonished him, "As supreme commander you should direct affairs with method — why must you personally face arrows and stones?"

sentences.zh: 」自四月至七月，乃屠城斬誕。

translations.literal: From the fourth month to the seventh, they finally sacked the city and executed Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Between the fourth month and the seventh, they finally sacked the city and executed Dan.

sentences.zh: 進慶之司空，又固讓爵。

translations.literal: Qingzhi was promoted to Minister of Works; again he firmly declined the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi then was promoted to Minister of Works; again he firmly declined the enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 於是與柳元景並依晉密陵侯鄭袤故事，朝會慶之位次司空，元景在從公之上，給恤吏五十人，門施行馬。

translations.literal: Thereupon he and Liu Yuanjing were both granted, following the precedent of Marquis Mi of Jin Zheng Mao, precedence at court equal to the Minister of Works for Qingzhi, with Yuanjing above the lesser dukes; fifty condolence officers and gate horses were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he and Liu Yuanjing were both granted, following the precedent of Marquis Mi of Jin, Zheng Mao, precedence at court equal to the Minister of Works for Qingzhi, with Yuanjing above the lesser dukes; fifty condolence officers and gate horses were granted.

sentences.zh: 初，慶之嘗夢引鹵簿入廁中，慶之甚惡入廁之鄙。

translations.literal: Initially Qingzhi once dreamed of leading an imperial procession into a privy; he greatly loathed the vulgarity of entering a privy.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Qingzhi once dreamed of leading an imperial procession into a privy; he greatly loathed the vulgarity of the image.

sentences.zh: 時有善占夢者為解之，曰：「君必大富貴，然未在旦夕。

translations.literal: At the time a skilled dream interpreter explained: "You will surely attain great wealth and honor, but not immediately."
translations.idiomatic: At the time a skilled dream interpreter explained, "You will surely attain great wealth and honor, but not immediately."

sentences.zh: 」問其故，答云：「鹵簿固是富貴容，廁中所謂後帝也。

translations.literal: Asked the reason, he answered: "An imperial procession is naturally the image of wealth and honor; a privy signifies a later emperor."
translations.idiomatic: Asked the reason, he answered, "An imperial procession is naturally the image of wealth and honor; a privy signifies a later emperor."

sentences.zh: 知君富貴不在今主。

translations.literal: I know your wealth and honor do not lie with the present ruler.
translations.idiomatic: I know your wealth and honor do not lie with the present ruler."

sentences.zh: 」及中興之功，自五校至是而登三事。

translations.literal: When the merit of restoring the dynasty was achieved, from Infantry Commandant he rose to the Three Grand Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Once the merit of restoring the dynasty was achieved, from Infantry Commandant he rose to the Three Grand Offices.

sentences.zh: 四年，西陽五水蠻復為寇，慶之以郡公統諸軍討平之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the Xiyang Wushui barbarians raided again; Qingzhi, as duke of the commandery, commanded all armies and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, the Xiyang Wushui tribes raided again. Qingzhi, as duke of the commandery, commanded all armies and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 慶之居清明門外，有宅四所，室宇甚麗。

translations.literal: Qingzhi lived outside the Qingming Gate, with four residences of splendid construction.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi then lived outside the Qingming Gate, with four residences of splendid construction.

sentences.zh: 又有園舍在婁湖，慶之一夜攜子孫徙居之，以宅還官，悉移親戚中表于婁湖，列門同閈焉。

translations.literal: He also had an estate at Lou Lake; one night he moved his children and grandchildren there, returned the residences to the government, and relocated all his kin and cousins to Lou Lake in adjoining households.
translations.idiomatic: He also had an estate at Lou Lake. One night he moved his children and grandchildren there, returned the city residences to the government, and relocated all his kin and cousins to Lou Lake in adjoining households.

sentences.zh: 廣開田園之業，每指地語人曰：「錢盡在此。

translations.literal: He greatly expanded his farming estates, and whenever he pointed at the land would say to people: "All the money is here."
translations.idiomatic: He greatly expanded his farming estates, and whenever he pointed at the land he would tell people, "All the money is right here."

sentences.zh: 」中興身享大國，家素富厚，產業累萬金，奴僮千計。

translations.literal: After the restoration he enjoyed a great fief; his family had long been wealthy, with property worth tens of thousands in gold and more than a thousand slaves and servants.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration he enjoyed a great fief. His family had long been wealthy, with property worth tens of thousands in gold and more than a thousand slaves and servants.

sentences.zh: 再獻錢千萬，谷萬斛，以始興封優近，求改封南海郡，不許。

translations.literal: He again offered ten million cash and ten thousand hu of grain; because his Shixing fief was too close to the capital he requested a transfer to Nanhai Commandery but was denied.
translations.idiomatic: He again offered ten million in cash and ten thousand hu of grain. Because his Shixing fief lay too close to the capital, he requested a transfer to Nanhai Commandery but was denied.

sentences.zh: 妓妾十數人，並美容工藝。

translations.literal: He had more than ten concubines, all beautiful and skilled in the arts.
translations.idiomatic: He possessed more than ten concubines, all beautiful and skilled in the arts.

sentences.zh: 慶之優遊無事，盡意歡愉，自非朝賀不出門。

translations.literal: Qingzhi lived at leisure with nothing to do, enjoying himself to the full; unless it was a court audience he did not leave home.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi lived at leisure with nothing to do, enjoying himself to the full. Unless it was a court audience, he did not leave home.

sentences.zh: 每從遊幸及校獵，據鞍陵厲，不異少壯。

translations.literal: Whenever he joined excursions or hunts, he sat his saddle boldly and fiercely, no different from a young man.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he joined excursions or hunts, he sat his saddle boldly and fiercely, no different from a young man.

sentences.zh: 太子妃上孝武金鏤匕箸及杅杓，上以賜慶之曰：「觴酌之賜，宜以大夫為先也。」

translations.literal: The crown prince's consort presented to Xiaowu golden carved spoons and chopsticks and ladles; the emperor bestowed them on Qingzhi saying: "In the gift of wine cups, the great officer should come first."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's consort presented to Xiaowu golden carved spoons, chopsticks, and ladles. The emperor bestowed them on Qingzhi, saying, "In the gift of wine cups, the great officer should come first."

sentences.zh: 上嘗歡飲，普令群臣賦詩，慶之粗有口辯，手不知書，每將署事，輒恨眼不識字。

translations.literal: Once when the emperor was feasting merrily he ordered all ministers to compose poems. Qingzhi had rough eloquence but could not write; whenever he was to sign documents he regretted that his eyes did not know characters.
translations.idiomatic: Once when the emperor was feasting merrily, he ordered all the ministers to compose poems. Qingzhi had rough eloquence but could not write; whenever he was to sign documents he regretted that his eyes did not know characters.

sentences.zh: 上逼令作詩，慶之曰：「臣不知書，請口授師伯。

translations.literal: The emperor pressed him to compose a poem; Qingzhi said: "Your servant does not know writing — please let me dictate to Master Bo."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pressed him to compose a poem. Qingzhi said, "Your servant does not know writing — please let me dictate to Master Bo."

sentences.zh: 」上即令顏師伯執筆。

translations.literal: The emperor had Yan Shibo take up the brush.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then had Yan Shibo take up the brush.

sentences.zh: 慶之口授之曰：「微生遇多幸，得逢時運昌。

translations.literal: Qingzhi dictated: "This humble life has met great fortune, encountering an age of flourishing fortune."
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi then dictated: "This humble life has met great fortune, encountering an age of flourishing fortune."

sentences.zh: 朽老筋力盡，徒步還南岡。

translations.literal: Decrepit and old, my strength is spent; on foot I return to the southern hill."
translations.idiomatic: Decrepit and old, my strength is spent. on foot I return to the southern hill."

sentences.zh: 辭榮此聖世，何愧張子房。

translations.literal: Renouncing glory in this sage age — what shame compared to Zhang Zifang?"
translations.idiomatic: Renouncing glory in this sage age, what shame compared to Zhang Zifang?"

sentences.zh: 」上甚悅，眾坐並稱其辭意之美。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased; all present praised the beauty of the verse.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased, and all present praised the beauty of the verse.

sentences.zh: 孝武晏駕，慶之與柳元景等並受顧命。

translations.literal: When Xiaowu died, Qingzhi along with Liu Yuanjing and others all received deathbed appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xiaowu died, Qingzhi along with Liu Yuanjing and others all received deathbed appointment.

sentences.zh: 遺制「若有大軍旅及征討，悉委慶之」。

translations.literal: The testamentary instructions read: "If there are major military campaigns or punitive expeditions, entrust them all to Qingzhi."
translations.idiomatic: The testamentary instructions read, "If there are major military campaigns or punitive expeditions, entrust them all to Qingzhi."

sentences.zh: 前廢帝即位，加慶之几杖，給三望車一乘。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor ascended, Qingzhi was granted a leaning staff and given one Three-Canopy carriage.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor ascended the throne, Qingzhi was granted a leaning staff and given one Three-Canopy carriage.

sentences.zh: 慶之每朝賀，常乘豬鼻無幰車，左右從者不過三五騎。

translations.literal: Each time Qingzhi attended court he rode a pig-nose carriage without canopy, with no more than three or five escorts.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Qingzhi attended court he rode a pig-nose carriage without canopy, with no more than three or five escorts.

sentences.zh: 履行園田，每農桑劇月，無人從行，遇之者不知三公也。

translations.literal: When he walked through his gardens and fields, during the busiest farming seasons no one accompanied him; those who met him did not know he was one of the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: When he walked through his gardens and fields, during the busiest farming seasons no one accompanied him. Those who met him did not know he was one of the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 及加三望車，謂人曰：「我每游履田園，有人時與馬成三，無人則與馬成二。

translations.literal: When the Three-Canopy carriage was granted, he said to people: "Whenever I stroll through my fields, if someone is with me there are three of us with the horse; if no one is with me there are two of us with the horse.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three-Canopy carriage was granted, he said to people, "Whenever I stroll through my fields, if someone is with me there are three of us with the horse; if no one is with me there are two of us with the horse.

sentences.zh: 今乘此車，安所之乎？

translations.literal: Now riding this carriage — where am I to go?"
translations.idiomatic: Now riding this carriage, where am I to go?"

sentences.zh: 」及賜几杖，並固讓。

translations.literal: When the leaning staff was granted, he again firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Once the leaning staff was granted, he again firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 柳元景、顏師伯嘗詣慶之，會其游田，元景等鳴笳列卒滿道，慶之獨與左右一人在田，見之悄然改容曰：「夫貧賤不可居，富貴亦難守。

translations.literal: Liu Yuanjing and Yan Shibo once came to visit Qingzhi and found him touring his fields; Yuanjing and the others sounded horns and lined soldiers filling the road, while Qingzhi was alone in the fields with one attendant. Seeing this he changed expression and said quietly: "Poverty and low station cannot be endured — yet wealth and honor are also hard to keep.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuanjing and Yan Shibo once came to visit Qingzhi and found him touring his fields. Yuanjing and the others sounded horns and lined soldiers filling the road, while Qingzhi was alone in the fields with one attendant. Seeing this he changed expression and said quietly, "Poverty and low station cannot be endured — yet wealth and honor are also hard to keep.

sentences.zh: 吾與諸公並出貧賤，因時際會，榮貴至此，唯當共思損挹之事。

translations.literal: You and I all rose from poverty and low station; through the times and chance we have reached such glory and honor — we ought only to think together of how to restrain ourselves.
translations.idiomatic: You and I all rose from poverty and low station. Through the times and chance we have reached such glory and honor — we ought only to think together of how to restrain ourselves.

sentences.zh: 老子八十之年，目見成敗者已多，諸君炫此車服，欲何為乎！

translations.literal: I am eighty years old and have seen many rises and falls; you gentlemen display these carriages and robes — what do you intend?"
translations.idiomatic: I am eighty years old and have seen many rises and falls. You gentlemen display these carriages and robes — what do you intend?"

sentences.zh: 」於是插杖而耘，不為之顧。

translations.literal: Thereupon he planted his staff and hoed, paying them no heed.
translations.idiomatic: At that point he planted his staff and hoed, paying them no heed.

sentences.zh: 元景等徹侍褰裳從之，慶之乃與相對為歡。

translations.literal: Yuanjing and the others dismissed attendants, lifted their robes and followed; Qingzhi then shared merriment with them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing and the others dismissed their attendants, lifted their robes and followed; Qingzhi then shared merriment with them.

sentences.zh: 慶之既通貴，鄉里老舊素輕慶之者，後見皆膝行而前。

translations.literal: Once Qingzhi had attained high rank, old acquaintances in the village who had once looked down on him now all came forward on their knees.
translations.idiomatic: Once Qingzhi had attained high rank, old acquaintances in the village who had once looked down on him now all came forward on their knees.

sentences.zh: 慶之歎曰：「故是昔時沈公。

translations.literal: Qingzhi sighed: "This is still the old Master Shen."
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi sighed, "This is still the old Master Shen."

sentences.zh: 」視諸沈為劫首者數十人，士民悉患之。

translations.literal: He saw several dozen Shen clansmen who were bandit leaders; gentry and commoners all suffered from them.
translations.idiomatic: He saw several dozen Shen clansmen who were bandit leaders. gentry and commoners all suffered from them.

sentences.zh: 慶之詭為置酒大會，一時殺之，於是合境肅清，人皆喜悅。

translations.literal: Qingzhi pretended to arrange a great feast and at one stroke killed them; the whole district was pacified and all rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi pretended to arrange a great feast and at one stroke killed them. The whole district was pacified and all rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 廢帝狂悖無道，眾勸之廢立，及柳元景等連謀，以告慶之，慶之與江夏王義恭不厚，發其事。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor was wildly wicked; many counseled deposing and replacing him. Liu Yuanjing and others conspired and told Qingzhi, but Qingzhi was not close to Prince Yixia of Jiangxia Liu Yigong and revealed the plot.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor was wildly wicked; many counseled deposing and replacing him. Liu Yuanjing and others conspired and told Qingzhi, but Qingzhi was not on good terms with Prince Yixia of Jiangxia Liu Yigong and revealed the plot.

sentences.zh: 帝誅義恭、元景等，以慶之為侍中、太尉。

translations.literal: The emperor executed Yigong, Yuanjing and others, and made Qingzhi Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor executed Yigong, Yuanjing, and others, and made Qingzhi Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 及義陽王昶反，慶之從帝度江，總統眾軍。

translations.literal: When Prince Chang of Yiyang rebelled, Qingzhi accompanied the emperor across the river and commanded all armies.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Chang of Yiyang rebelled, Qingzhi accompanied the emperor across the river and commanded all the armies.

sentences.zh: 帝凶暴日甚，慶之猶盡言諫爭，帝意稍不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor grew daily more cruel; Qingzhi still remonstrated fully, and the emperor grew somewhat displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew daily more cruel. Qingzhi still remonstrated fully, and the emperor grew somewhat displeased.

sentences.zh: 及誅何邁，慮慶之不同，量其必至，乃開青溪諸橋以絕之。

translations.literal: When He Mai was executed, fearing Qingzhi would not agree and calculating he would surely come, the emperor opened the Qingxi bridges to cut him off.
translations.idiomatic: When He Mai was executed, fearing Qingzhi would not agree and calculating that he would surely come, the emperor opened the Qingxi bridges to cut him off.

sentences.zh: 慶之果往，不得度而還。

translations.literal: Qingzhi did come but could not cross and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi then did come but could not cross and returned.

sentences.zh: 帝又忌之，乃遣其從子攸之齎藥賜死，時年八十。

translations.literal: The emperor also envied him and sent his nephew Youzhi with poison to grant death; he was eighty years old.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also envied him and sent his nephew Youzhi with poison to grant death. He was eighty years old.

sentences.zh: 是歲旦，慶之夢有人以兩疋絹與之，謂曰：「此絹足度。

translations.literal: That New Year's Day Qingzhi dreamed someone gave him two bolts of silk, saying: "This silk is just enough in length."
translations.idiomatic: That New Year's Day Qingzhi dreamed someone gave him two bolts of silk, saying, "This silk is just enough in length."

sentences.zh: 」寤而謂人曰：「老子今年不免矣。

translations.literal: Awakening he told people: "This old man will not escape this year."
translations.idiomatic: Awakening, he told people, "This old man will not escape this year."

sentences.zh: 兩疋，八十尺也，足度，無盈餘矣。

translations.literal: Two bolts — eighty feet; enough in length, with no surplus."
translations.idiomatic: Two bolts — eighty feet. enough in length, with no surplus."

sentences.zh: 」及死，贈賻甚厚，追贈侍中、太尉如故，給鸞輅轀輬車，前後羽葆、鼓吹，諡曰忠武公。

translations.literal: Upon death, generous funeral gifts were granted; he was posthumously enfeoffed Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Commandant as before, given an imperial hearse with carriage and canopy, front and rear feather banners and drums, with posthumous title Duke Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Upon death, generous funeral gifts were granted. He was posthumously enfeoffed Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Commandant as before, given an imperial hearse with carriage and canopy, front and rear feather banners and drums, with the posthumous title Duke Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 未及葬，帝敗。

translations.literal: Before burial the emperor was overthrown.
translations.idiomatic: Before burial could take place, the emperor was overthrown.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，追贈侍中、司空，諡曰襄公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended, he was posthumously enfeoffed Attendant-in-Ordinary and Minister of Works, with posthumous title Duke Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, he was posthumously enfeoffed Attendant-in-Ordinary and Minister of Works, with the posthumous title Duke Xiang.

sentences.zh: 泰始七年，改封蒼梧郡公。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taishi, his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Cangwu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Taishi, his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Cangwu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 慶之群從姻戚，由慶之在列位者數十人。

translations.literal: Dozens of Qingzhi's kinsmen by marriage held office through his rank.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of Qingzhi's kinsmen by marriage held office through his rank.

sentences.zh: 長子文叔位侍中，慶之之死也，不肯飲藥，攸之以被掩殺之，文叔密取藥藏錄。

translations.literal: His eldest son Wenshu held the post of Attendant-in-Ordinary; at Qingzhi's death Wenshu refused to drink the poison. Youzhi smothered him with a quilt; Wenshu secretly took the drug and preserved a record of it.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Wenshu held the post of Attendant-in-Ordinary. At Qingzhi's death Wenshu refused to drink the poison. Youzhi smothered him with a quilt; Wenshu secretly took the drug and preserved a record of it.

sentences.zh: 或勸文叔逃避，文叔見帝斷截江夏王義恭支體，慮奔亡之日，帝怒，容致義恭之變，乃飲藥自殺。

translations.literal: Some urged Wenshu to flee; Wenshu saw the emperor cut apart Prince Yixia of Jiangxia Liu Yigong limb by limb and feared that if he fled the emperor's wrath might bring disaster like Yigong's — so he drank the poison and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Wenshu to flee. Wenshu saw the emperor cut apart Prince Yixia of Jiangxia Liu Yigong limb by limb and feared that if he fled, the emperor's wrath might bring disaster like Yigong's — so he drank the poison and killed himself.

sentences.zh: 文叔子昭明位秘書郎，聞父死，曰：「何忍獨生。

translations.literal: Wenshu's son Zhaoming held the post of Secretary; hearing of his father's death he said: "How can I bear to live alone."
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu's son Zhaoming held the post of Secretary. Hearing of his father's death he said, "How can I bear to live alone?"

sentences.zh: 」亦自縊死。

translations.literal: He too hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: He also hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 昭略字茂隆，性狂俊，不事公卿，使酒仗氣，無所推下。

translations.literal: Zhaolue, styled Maolong, was wild and brilliant, deferring to no grandees; he drank freely, relied on his spirit, and bowed to no one.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaolue, styled Maolong, was wild and brilliant, deferring to no grandees. He drank freely, relied on his spirit, and bowed to no one.

sentences.zh: 嘗醉，晚日負杖攜家賓子弟至婁湖苑，逢王景文子約，張目視之曰：「汝是王約邪？

translations.literal: Once when drunk, at late afternoon he shouldered a staff and led household guests and younger kinsmen to the Lou Lake park, where he met Wang Jingwen's son Yue. He stared and said: "Are you Wang Yue?
translations.idiomatic: Once when drunk, at late afternoon he shouldered a staff and led household guests and younger kinsmen to the Lou Lake park, where he met Wang Jingwen's son Yue. He stared and said, "Are you Wang Yue?

sentences.zh: 何乃肥而癡。

translations.literal: Why are you so fat and stupid."
translations.idiomatic: Why are you so fat and stupid?"

sentences.zh: 」約曰：「汝沈昭略邪？

translations.literal: Yue said: "Are you Shen Zhaolue?
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, "Are you Shen Zhaolue?

sentences.zh: 何乃瘦而狂。

translations.literal: Why are you so thin and mad."
translations.idiomatic: Why are you so thin and mad?"

sentences.zh: 」昭略撫掌大笑曰：「瘦已勝肥，狂又勝癡，奈何王約，奈汝癡何！」

translations.literal: Zhaolue clapped his hands and laughed loudly: "Thin already beats fat, and mad already beats stupid — what can you do, Wang Yue? What can you do about your stupidity!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhaolue clapped his hands and laughed loudly, "Thin already beats fat, and mad already beats stupid — what can you do, Wang Yue? What can you do about your stupidity!"

sentences.zh: 永元中，與叔父文季俱被召入華林省，茹法珍等進藥酒，昭略怒駡徐孝嗣曰：「廢昏立明，古今令典，宰相無才，致有今日。

translations.literal: In the Yongyuan era he and his uncle Wenji were both summoned into the Hualin Palace; Ru Fazhen and others brought poisoned wine. Zhaolue angrily cursed Xu Xiaosi: "Deposing the wicked and establishing the enlightened is the fine precedent of past and present — yet the chancellor lacked talent and brought about this day."
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongyuan era he and his uncle Wenji were both summoned into the Hualin Palace; Ru Fazhen and others brought poisoned wine. Zhaolue angrily cursed Xu Xiaosi, "Deposing the wicked and establishing the enlightened is the fine precedent of past and present — yet the chancellor lacked talent and brought about this day."

sentences.zh: 」以甌投其面，曰：「使為破面鬼。

translations.literal: He threw a bowl at his face, saying: "May you become a face-smashing ghost."
translations.idiomatic: He threw a bowl at his face, saying, "May you become a face-smashing ghost."

sentences.zh: 」死時言笑自若，了無懼容。

translations.literal: At death he spoke and laughed as if at ease, with no trace of fear.
translations.idiomatic: Facing death he spoke and laughed as if at ease, with no trace of fear.

sentences.zh: 徐孝嗣謂曰：「見卿使人想夏侯泰初。

translations.literal: Xu Xiaosi said to him: "Seeing you makes one think of Xiahou Tai Chu."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xiaosi said to him, "Seeing you makes one think of Xiahou Tai Chu."

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「明府猶憶夏侯，便是方寸不能都豁。

translations.literal: He answered: "Your Excellency still remembers Xiahou — so your heart cannot be entirely open.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Your Excellency still remembers Xiahou — so your heart cannot be entirely open.

sentences.zh: 下官見龍逄、比干，欣然相對；

translations.literal: Your humble servant, seeing Long Feng and Bi Gan, would gladly face them as equals;
translations.idiomatic: Your humble servant, seeing Long Feng and Bi Gan, would gladly face them as equals;.

sentences.zh: 霍光脫問明府今日之事，何辭答之邪？」

translations.literal: If Huo Guang were freed to question you, what words would Your Excellency use to answer him today?"
translations.idiomatic: If Huo Guang were freed to question you, what words would Your Excellency use to answer him today?"

sentences.zh: 昭略弟昭光聞收兵至，家人勸逃去，昭光不忍舍母，入執母手悲泣，遂見殺。

translations.literal: Zhaolue's younger brother Zhaoguang, hearing arresting troops had come, was urged by his family to flee; Zhaoguang could not bear to leave his mother, entered and grasped her hand weeping, and was then killed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaolue's younger brother Zhaoguang, hearing arresting troops had come, was urged by his family to flee. Zhaoguang could not bear to leave his mother, entered and grasped her hand weeping, and was then killed.

sentences.zh: 時昭明子曇亮已得逃去，聞昭光死，乃曰：「家門屠滅，獨用生何為。

translations.literal: At the time Zhaoming's son Tanliang had already escaped; hearing of Zhaoguang's death he said: "The household is slaughtered to the last — what use is living alone."
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhaoming's son Tanliang had already escaped. Hearing of Zhaoguang's death he said, "The household is slaughtered to the last — what use is living alone?"

sentences.zh: 」又絕吭而死。

translations.literal: He too cut his throat and died.
translations.idiomatic: He also cut his throat and died.

sentences.zh: 時人歎其累世孝義。

translations.literal: People of the time praised their generations of filial righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Men of the time praised their generations of filial righteousness.

sentences.zh: 中興元年，贈昭略太常，昭光廷尉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongxing, Zhaolue was posthumously enfeoffed Minister of Ceremonies and Zhaoguang Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongxing, Zhaolue was posthumously enfeoffed Minister of Ceremonies and Zhaoguang Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 文季字仲達，文叔弟也。

translations.literal: Wenji, styled Zhongda, was Wenshu's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Wenji, styled Zhongda, was the younger brother of Wenshu.

sentences.zh: 以寬雅正直見知，尤善塞及彈碁，在宋封山陽縣五等伯，位中書郎。

translations.literal: Known for his generous integrity and uprightness, he was especially skilled at go and pitch-pot; under Song he was enfeoffed Fifth-Rank Baron of Shanyang county and held the post of Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Known for his generous integrity and uprightness, he was especially skilled at go and pitch-pot. Under Song he was enfeoffed Fifth-Rank Baron of Shanyang county and held the post of Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 父慶之遇害，諸子見收，文叔謂之曰：「我能死，爾能報。

translations.literal: When father Qingzhi was murdered and the sons were arrested, Wenshu told him: "I can die; you can avenge."
translations.idiomatic: When father Qingzhi was murdered and the sons were arrested, Wenshu told him, "I can die; you can avenge."

sentences.zh: 」遂自殺。

translations.literal: Thereupon he killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: At that point he killed himself.

sentences.zh: 文季揮刀馳馬去，收者不敢追，遂免。

translations.literal: Wenji waved a blade and galloped away; the arresters did not dare pursue and he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Wenji waved a blade and galloped away. The arresters did not dare pursue, and he escaped.

sentences.zh: 文季風采棱岸，善於進止，司徒褚彥回當時貴望，頗以門戶裁之。

translations.literal: Wenji's bearing was stern and lofty, skilled in deportment; Chu Yanhui, then the most honored man of the age, somewhat measured him by family status.
translations.idiomatic: Wenji's bearing was stern and lofty, skilled in deportment. Chu Yanhui, then the most honored man of the age, somewhat measured him by family status.

sentences.zh: 文季不為之屈。

translations.literal: Wenji did not yield to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenji then did not yield to him.

sentences.zh: 武帝在東宮，于玄圃宴朝臣，文季數舉酒勸彥回。

translations.literal: When the Emperor Wu was in the Eastern Palace he held a banquet for court ministers in the Mystic Garden; Wenji repeatedly raised his cup to urge Yanhui to drink.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu was in the Eastern Palace he held a banquet for court ministers in the Mystic Garden. Wenji repeatedly raised his cup to urge Yanhui to drink.

sentences.zh: 彥回甚不平，啟武帝曰：「沈文季謂彥回經為其郡，依然猶有故情。

translations.literal: Yanhui was greatly displeased and reported to the emperor: "Shen Wenji says Yanhui was once his commandery administrator and still retains old affection."
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui was greatly displeased and reported to the emperor, "Shen Wenji says Yanhui was once his commandery administrator and still retains old affection."

sentences.zh: 」文季曰：「惟桑與梓，必恭敬止。

translations.literal: Wenji said: "Only the mulberry and catalpa — one must approach with reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Wenji said, "Only the mulberry and catalpa — one must approach with reverence.

sentences.zh: 豈如明府亡國失土，不識枌榆。

translations.literal: How unlike Your Excellency, who lost your state and land and no longer knows your native elm and pine."
translations.idiomatic: How unlike Your Excellency, who lost your state and land and no longer knows your native elm and pine.".

sentences.zh: 」遂言及魏軍動事。

translations.literal: Thereupon the talk turned to Wei army movements.
translations.idiomatic: At that point the talk turned to Wei army movements.

sentences.zh: 彥回曰：「陳顯達、沈文季當今將略，足委以邊事。

translations.literal: Yanhui said: "Chen Xianda and Shen Wenji are the present masters of strategy — fully fit to be entrusted with frontier affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui said, "Chen Xianda and Shen Wenji are the present masters of strategy — fully fit to be entrusted with frontier affairs."

sentences.zh: 」文季諱稱將門，因是發怒，啟武帝曰：「褚彥回遂品藻人流，臣未知其身死之日，何面目見宋明帝。

translations.literal: Wenji disliked being called a general's house and grew angry; he reported to the emperor: "Chu Yanhui goes so far as to judge men's character — your servant does not know on the day of his own death with what face he can meet Emperor Ming of Song."
translations.idiomatic: Wenji disliked being called a general's house and grew angry. He reported to the emperor, "Chu Yanhui goes so far as to judge men's character — your servant does not know on the day of his own death with what face he can meet Emperor Ming of Song."

sentences.zh: 」武帝笑曰：「沈率醉也。

translations.literal: The emperor laughed and said: "Shen is simply drunk."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and said, "Shen is simply drunk."

sentences.zh: 」中丞劉休舉其事，見原。

translations.literal: Censor Liu Xiu memorialized the matter; Wenji was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Liu Xiu memorialized the matter. Wenji was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 後豫章王北宅後堂集會，文季與彥回並善琵琶，酒闌，彥回取樂器為明君曲。

translations.literal: Later at a gathering in the rear hall of Prince of Yuzhang's northern residence, Wenji and Yanhui were both skilled at the pipa; when the wine had gone around Yanhui took up the instrument and played the Bright Consort melody.
translations.idiomatic: Later at a gathering in the rear hall of the Prince of Yuzhang's northern residence, Wenji and Yanhui were both skilled at the pipa. When the wine had gone around, Yanhui took up the instrument and played the Bright Consort melody.

sentences.zh: 文季便下席大唱曰：「沈文季不能作伎兒。

translations.literal: Wenji left his seat and sang loudly: "Shen Wenji cannot play the entertainer."
translations.idiomatic: Wenji left his seat and sang loudly, "Shen Wenji cannot play the entertainer."

sentences.zh: 」豫章王嶷又解之曰：「此故當不損仲容之德。

translations.literal: Prince of Yuzhang Jiong also smoothed things over: "This surely does not diminish Zhongrong's virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yuzhang Jiong also smoothed things over, saying, "This surely does not diminish Zhongrong's virtue."

sentences.zh: 」彥回顏色無異，終曲而止。

translations.literal: Yanhui's expression did not change; he played to the end and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui's expression did not change. he played to the end and stopped.

sentences.zh: 永明中，累遷領軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the Yongming era he was repeatedly promoted to General of the Palace Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongming era, he was repeatedly promoted to General of the Palace Attendants.

sentences.zh: 文季雖不學，發言必有辭采。

translations.literal: Though Wenji did not study, whenever he spoke his words had literary color.
translations.idiomatic: Though Wenji did not study, whenever he spoke his words had literary color.

sentences.zh: 武帝謂文季曰：「南士無僕射，多歷年所。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Wenji: "Southern men have gone many years without a Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Wenji, "Southern men have gone many years without a Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 」文季對曰：「南風不競，非復一日。

translations.literal: Wenji replied: "The southern wind does not prevail — this is no affair of a single day."
translations.idiomatic: Wenji replied, "The southern wind does not prevail — this is no affair of a single day."

sentences.zh: 」當世善其對。

translations.literal: Contemporaries praised his reply.
translations.idiomatic: Men of the time praised his reply.

sentences.zh: 建武二年，魏軍南伐，明帝以為憂，制文季鎮壽春。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu the Wei army marched south to attack; Emperor Ming was troubled and ordered Wenji to garrison Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianwu the Wei army marched south to attack. Emperor Ming was troubled and ordered Wenji to garrison Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 文季入，城門嚴加備守。

translations.literal: Wenji entered and the city gates were strictly fortified.
translations.idiomatic: Wenji then entered and the city gates were strictly fortified.

sentences.zh: 魏軍尋退，百姓無所損。

translations.literal: The Wei army soon withdrew; the common people suffered no harm.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei army soon withdrew. the common people suffered no harm.

sentences.zh: 永元元年，轉侍中、左僕射。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongyuan he was transferred to Attendant-in-Ordinary and Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongyuan he was transferred to Attendant-in-Ordinary and Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 始安王遙光反，其夜遣於宅掩取文季，欲以為都督，而文季已還台。

translations.literal: When Prince Yao Guang of Shi'an rebelled, that night he sent men to Wenji's residence to seize him, intending to make him grand commander; but Wenji had already returned to the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Once Prince Yao Guang of Shi'an rebelled, that night he sent men to Wenji's residence to seize him, intending to make him grand commander; but Wenji had already returned to the ministry.

sentences.zh: 明日，與尚書令徐孝嗣共坐南掖門上。

translations.literal: The next day he sat with Chief Minister Xu Xiaosi on the Southern Side Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he sat with Chief Minister Xu Xiaosi on the Southern Side Gate.

sentences.zh: 時東昏已行殺戮，孝嗣深懷憂慮，欲與文季論時事，文季輒引以他辭，終不得及。

translations.literal: By then Dong Hun had already begun the slaughter; Xiaosi was deeply troubled and wished to discuss current affairs with Wenji, but Wenji always turned the talk elsewhere and never reached the subject.
translations.idiomatic: By then Dong Hun had already begun the slaughter. Xiaosi was deeply troubled and wished to discuss current affairs with Wenji, but Wenji always turned the talk elsewhere and never reached the subject.

sentences.zh: 事甯，加鎮軍將軍，置府史。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the Army and given a headquarters staff.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was settled he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the Army and given a headquarters staff.

sentences.zh: 文季以時方昏亂，托老疾不豫朝機。

translations.literal: Wenji, seeing the times were chaotic and corrupt, pleaded old age and illness to avoid court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wenji, seeing the times were chaotic and corrupt, pleaded old age and illness to avoid court affairs.

sentences.zh: 兄子昭略謂文季曰：「阿父年六十為員外僕射，欲求免乎？

translations.literal: His nephew Zhaolue said to Wenji: "Uncle, at sixty you are Supernumerary Vice Director — do you wish to be spared?"
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Zhaolue said to Wenji, "Uncle, at sixty you are Supernumerary Vice Director — do you wish to be spared?"

sentences.zh: 」文季笑而不答，未幾見害。

translations.literal: Wenji smiled and did not answer; before long he was murdered.
translations.idiomatic: Wenji smiled and did not answer. Before long he was murdered.

sentences.zh: 先被召，便知敗，舉動如常。

translations.literal: When first summoned he already knew of defeat; his conduct was as usual.
translations.idiomatic: When first summoned he already knew of defeat. his conduct was as usual.

sentences.zh: 登車顧曰：「此行恐往而不反。

translations.literal: Mounting his carriage he looked back and said: "This journey — I fear I go but do not return."
translations.idiomatic: Mounting his carriage he looked back and said, "This journey — I fear I go but do not return."

sentences.zh: 」于華林省死，年五十八，朝野冤之。

translations.literal: He died in the Hualin Palace at age fifty-eight; court and commoners alike considered it an injustice.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the Hualin Palace at age fifty-eight. Court and commoners alike considered it an injustice.

sentences.zh: 中興元年，贈司空，諡曰忠憲公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongxing he was posthumously enfeoffed Minister of Works with posthumous title Duke Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongxing he was posthumously enfeoffed Minister of Works with the posthumous title Duke Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 文秀字仲遠，慶之弟子也。

translations.literal: Wenxiu, styled Zhongyuan, was Qingzhi's nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu, styled Zhongyuan, was Qingzhi's nephew by blood.

sentences.zh: 父邵之，南中郎行參軍。

translations.literal: His father Shaozhi was Acting Adjutant in the Southern Central Office.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shaozhi served as Acting Adjutant in the Southern Central Office.

sentences.zh: 文秀宋前廢帝時，累遷青州刺史，將之鎮，部曲出次白下。

translations.literal: Under the Deposed Emperor of Song Wenxiu was repeatedly promoted to Inspector of Qing Province; going to his post, his troops encamped at Baixia.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Deposed Emperor of Song Wenxiu was repeatedly promoted to Inspector of Qing Province. Going to his post, his troops encamped at Baixia.

sentences.zh: 文秀說慶之以帝狂悖，禍在難測，欲因此眾力圖之。

translations.literal: Wenxiu urged Qingzhi that the emperor was wildly wicked and disaster was hard to foretell, wishing to use this force to plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu urged Qingzhi that the emperor was wildly wicked and disaster was hard to foretell, wishing to use this force to plot against him.

sentences.zh: 慶之不從。

translations.literal: Qingzhi did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi then did not consent.

sentences.zh: 及行，慶之果見殺。

translations.literal: When Wenxiu departed, Qingzhi was indeed murdered.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wenxiu departed, Qingzhi was indeed murdered.

sentences.zh: 又遣直閣江方興領兵誅文秀，未至，而明帝已定亂。

translations.literal: The court also sent Palace Attendant Jiang Fangxing with troops to execute Wenxiu; before he arrived Emperor Ming had already settled the turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: The court also sent Palace Attendant Jiang Fangxing with troops to execute Wenxiu. Before he arrived, Emperor Ming had already settled the turmoil.

sentences.zh: 時晉安王子勳據尋陽，文秀與徐州刺史薛安都並同子勳反。

translations.literal: At the time Prince Zixun of Jin'an held Xunyang; Wenxiu and Xue Andu, Inspector of Xu Province, both joined Zixun in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Prince Zixun of Jin'an held Xunyang. Wenxiu and Xue Andu, Inspector of Xu Province, both joined Zixun in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 尋陽平定，明帝遣其弟召之，便歸命請罪。

translations.literal: When Xunyang was pacified Emperor Ming sent his younger brother to summon Wenxiu; he at once submitted and pleaded guilty.
translations.idiomatic: When Xunyang was pacified, Emperor Ming sent his younger brother to summon Wenxiu. He at once submitted and pleaded guilty.

sentences.zh: 即安本任。

translations.literal: He was immediately restored to his original post.
translations.idiomatic: He became immediately restored to his original post.

sentences.zh: 四年，封新城縣侯。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was enfeoffed Marquis of Xincheng county.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was enfeoffed Marquis of Xincheng county.

sentences.zh: 先是冀州刺史崔道固亦據曆城同反，文秀遣信引魏，魏遣慕容白曜援之。

translations.literal: Earlier Inspector of Ji Province Cui Daogu had also held Licheng in rebellion; Wenxiu sent envoys to summon Wei aid, and Wei sent Murong Baizhao to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Inspector of Ji Province Cui Daogu had also held Licheng in rebellion. Wenxiu sent envoys to summon Wei aid, and Wei sent Murong Baizhao to assist.

sentences.zh: 及至，而文秀已受朝命。

translations.literal: When Baizhao arrived Wenxiu had already accepted the court's appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When Baizhao arrived Wenxiu had already accepted the court's appointment.

sentences.zh: 文秀善於撫禦，被魏圍三載無叛者。

translations.literal: Wenxiu was skilled at comforting and controlling troops; besieged by Wei for three years none defected.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu was skilled at comforting and controlling troops. Besieged by Wei for three years, none defected.

sentences.zh: 五年，為魏所克，終於北。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was taken by Wei and died in the north.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was taken by Wei and died in the north.

sentences.zh: 攸之字仲達，慶之從父兄子也。

translations.literal: Youzhi, styled Zhongda, was Qingzhi's cousin's son.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi, styled Zhongda, was the son of Qingzhi's cousin.

sentences.zh: 父叔仁為宋衡陽王義季征西長史，兼行參軍領隊。

translations.literal: His father Shuren was Chief Administrator on the Western Campaigning staff of Prince Yiji of Hengyang and concurrently Acting Adjutant leading a guard unit.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shuren served as Chief Administrator on the Western Campaigning staff of Prince Yiji of Hengyang and concurrently as Acting Adjutant leading a guard unit.

sentences.zh: 攸之少孤貧，元嘉二十七年，魏軍南攻，朝廷發三吳之眾，攸之亦行。

translations.literal: Youzhi was orphaned and poor in youth. In the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia the Wei army attacked south; the court mobilized the Three Wu regions and Youzhi also went.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi was orphaned and poor in youth. In the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia the Wei army attacked south. The court mobilized the Three Wu regions and Youzhi also went.

sentences.zh: 及至建鄴，詣領軍將軍劉遵考求補白丁隊主。

translations.literal: Upon reaching Jiankang he went to General of the Palace Attendants Liu Zunkao requesting appointment as squad leader of common conscripts.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching Jiankang he went to General of the Palace Attendants Liu Zunkao requesting appointment as squad leader of common conscripts.

sentences.zh: 遵考以為形陋不堪，攸之歎曰：「昔孟嘗君身長六尺為齊相，今求士取肥大者哉。

translations.literal: Zunkao thought his appearance ugly and unsuitable; Youzhi sighed: "In old times Lord Mengchang, though only six feet tall, became Chancellor of Qi — do you seek men by size alone?"
translations.idiomatic: Zunkao thought his appearance ugly and unsuitable. Youzhi sighed, "In old times Lord Mengchang, though only six feet tall, became Chancellor of Qi — do you seek men by size alone?"

sentences.zh: 」因隨慶之征討。

translations.literal: Thereupon he followed Qingzhi on campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: At that point he followed Qingzhi on campaigns.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，征西陽蠻，始補隊主。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, campaigning against the Xiyang tribes, he was first appointed squad leader.
translations.idiomatic: During the twenty-ninth year, campaigning against the Xiyang tribes, he was first appointed squad leader.

sentences.zh: 巴口建義，授南中郎府板長兼行參軍。

translations.literal: At the righteous rising at Bakou he was given provisional appointment as Senior Adjutant in the Southern Central Office with concurrent Acting Adjutant duties.
translations.idiomatic: At the righteous rising at Bakou he was given provisional appointment as Senior Adjutant in the Southern Central Office with concurrent Acting Adjutant duties.

sentences.zh: 新亭之戰，身被重創，事甯，為太尉行參軍，封平洛縣五等侯。

translations.literal: At the battle of Xinting he received grave wounds; when the affair was settled he became Acting Adjutant to the Grand Commandant and was enfeoffed Fifth-Rank Marquis of Pingluo county.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Xinting he received grave wounds. When the affair was settled he became Acting Adjutant to the Grand Commandant and was enfeoffed Fifth-Rank Marquis of Pingluo county.

sentences.zh: 隨府轉大司馬行參軍。

translations.literal: He transferred with the headquarters to Acting Adjutant to the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He transferred with the headquarters to Acting Adjutant to the Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 晉時都下二岸揚州舊置都部從事，分掌二縣非違，永初以後罷省。

translations.literal: In Jin times the capital's two riverbanks had a Capital Bureau Attendant under Yang Province to oversee violations in the two counties; after Yongchu this post was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin times the capital's two riverbanks had a Capital Bureau Attendant under Yang Province to oversee violations in the two counties. After Yongchu this post was abolished.

sentences.zh: 孝建三年，復置其職，攸之掌北岸，會稽孔璪掌南岸，後又罷。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiaojian it was restored; Youzhi managed the north bank and Kong Zuan of Kuaiji the south bank; later it was again abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xiaojian it was restored. Youzhi managed the north bank and Kong Zuan of Kuaiji the south bank. Later it was again abolished.

sentences.zh: 攸之遷員外散騎侍郎，又隨慶之征廣陵屢有功，被箭破骨。

translations.literal: Youzhi was transferred to Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant at Leisure and again followed Qingzhi campaigning at Guangling with repeated merit, an arrow shattering his bone.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi then was transferred to Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant at Leisure and again followed Qingzhi campaigning at Guangling with repeated merit, an arrow shattering his bone.

sentences.zh: 孝武以其善戰，配以仇池步矟。

translations.literal: Xiaowu, because he fought well, paired him with a Qiu Chi infantry lance.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu, because he fought well, paired him with a Qiu Chi infantry lance.

sentences.zh: 事平當加厚賞，為慶之所抑。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he should have received generous reward but was held back by Qingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was settled he should have received generous reward but was held back by Qingzhi.

sentences.zh: 遷太子旅賁中郎，攸之甚恨之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Central Palace Guard of the Crown Prince's Rapid Tiger Guard; Youzhi deeply resented this.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Central Palace Guard of the Crown Prince's Rapid Tiger Guard. Youzhi deeply resented this.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝景和元年，除豫章王子尚車騎中兵參軍、直合，與宗越、譚金等並為廢帝所寵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jinghe of the Deposed Emperor he was appointed Middle Army Adjutant to Prince Zishang of Yuzhang's Chariots and Cavalry and Palace Attendant; with Zong Yue, Tan Jin and others he was all favored by the Deposed Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jinghe of the Deposed Emperor he was appointed Middle Army Adjutant to Prince Zishang of Yuzhang's Chariots and Cavalry and Palace Attendant. With Zong Yue, Tan Jin, and others he was all favored by the Deposed Emperor.

sentences.zh: 誅戮群公，攸之等皆為之用命，封東興縣侯。

translations.literal: In the execution of the grandees Youzhi and the others all obeyed orders; he was enfeoffed Marquis of Dongxing county.
translations.idiomatic: In the execution of the grandees Youzhi and the others all obeyed orders. He was enfeoffed Marquis of Dongxing county.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，以例削封。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended, his enfeoffment was reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, his enfeoffment was reduced by precedent.

sentences.zh: 尋告宗越、譚金等謀反，復召直合。

translations.literal: Soon he reported Zong Yue, Tan Jin and others for plotting rebellion and was again recalled as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he reported Zong Yue, Tan Jin, and others for plotting rebellion and was again recalled as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 會四方反叛，南賊已次近道，以攸之為甯朔將軍、尋陽太守，率軍據虎檻。

translations.literal: When rebellion broke out on all sides and southern rebels had nearly reached the road, Youzhi was made General Who Pacifies the North and Administrator of Xunyang, leading troops to hold Tiger Cage.
