translations.idiomatic: Once rebellion broke out on all sides and southern rebels had nearly reached the road, Youzhi was made General Who Pacifies the North and Administrator of Xunyang, leading troops to hold Tiger Cage.

sentences.zh: 時王玄謨為大統未發，前鋒有五軍在虎檻，五軍後又駱驛繼至，每夜各立姓號，不相稟受。

translations.literal: Wang Xuamo was grand commander but had not yet set out; the vanguard had five armies at Tiger Cage, and after the five armies more troops arrived in rapid succession, each night setting up their own surnames and titles without reporting to one another.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuamo was grand commander but had not yet set out. The vanguard had five armies at Tiger Cage, and after the five armies more troops arrived in rapid succession. Each night they set up their own surnames and titles without reporting to one another.

sentences.zh: 攸之謂軍吏曰：「今眾軍同舉，而姓號不同，若有耕夫漁父夜相呵叱，便致駭亂，此敗道也。

translations.literal: Youzhi told the army clerks: "Now all armies rise together yet bear different names and titles — if a farmer or fisherman shouted at night it would cause panic. This is the road to defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi told the army clerks, "Now all armies rise together yet bear different names and titles — if a farmer or fisherman shouted at night it would cause panic. This is the road to defeat.

sentences.zh: 請就一軍取號。

translations.literal: Please take one army's name for all."
translations.idiomatic: Please take one army's name for all.".

sentences.zh: 」眾咸從之。

translations.literal: All agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone agreed.

sentences.zh: 殷孝祖為前鋒都督，大失人情，攸之內撫將士，外諧群帥，眾並安之。

translations.literal: Yin Xiaozu was vanguard commander and greatly lost men's hearts; Youzhi comforted troops within and harmonized with commanders without, and all were reassured.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Xiaozu was vanguard commander and greatly lost men's hearts. Youzhi comforted troops within and harmonized with commanders without, and all were reassured.

sentences.zh: 時殷孝祖中流矢死，軍主範潛率五百人投賊，人情震駭，並謂攸之宜代孝祖為統。

translations.literal: When Xiaozu was struck by a stray arrow and died, army commander Fan Qian led five hundred men to defect to the rebels; men's hearts were shaken and all said Youzhi ought to replace Xiaozu as commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozu was struck by a stray arrow and died, army commander Fan Qian led five hundred men to defect to the rebels. Men's hearts were shaken and all said Youzhi ought to replace Xiaozu as commander.

sentences.zh: 時建安王休仁屯虎檻，總統眾軍，聞孝祖死，遣甯朔將軍江方興、龍驤將軍劉靈遺各率三千人赴赭圻。

translations.literal: Prince Xiuren of Jian'an was encamped at Tiger Cage commanding all armies; hearing of Xiaozu's death he sent General Who Pacifies the North Jiang Fangxing and Dragon Cavalry General Liu Lingyi each with three thousand men to Zhuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiuren of Jian'an was encamped at Tiger Cage commanding all armies. Hearing of Xiaozu's death he sent General Who Pacifies the North Jiang Fangxing and Dragon Cavalry General Liu Lingyi each with three thousand men to Zhuzhi.

sentences.zh: 攸之以為孝祖既死，賊有乘勝之心，明日若不更攻，則示之以弱。

translations.literal: Youzhi thought that with Xiaozu dead the rebels would have the mind to press their advantage; if they did not attack again tomorrow it would show weakness.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi thought that with Xiaozu dead the rebels would have the mind to press their advantage. If they did not attack again tomorrow it would show weakness.

sentences.zh: 方興名位相亞，必不為己下，軍政不一，致敗之由，乃率諸軍主詣方興推重，並慰勉之，方興甚悅。

translations.literal: Fangxing's name and rank were nearly equal and he would surely not serve under Youzhi; divided military authority was the cause of defeat — so he led all army commanders to Fangxing to honor and encourage him; Fangxing was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Fangxing's name and rank were nearly equal and he would surely not serve under Youzhi. Divided military authority was the cause of defeat — so he led all army commanders to Fangxing to honor and encourage him. Fangxing was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 攸之既出，諸軍主並尤之。

translations.literal: Once Youzhi had gone out all the army commanders blamed him.
translations.idiomatic: Once Youzhi had gone out all the army commanders blamed him.

sentences.zh: 攸之曰：「卿忘廉藺、寇賈事邪？

translations.literal: Youzhi said: "Have you forgotten Lian Po and Lin Xiangru, Kou Xun and Jia Fu?
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi said, "Have you forgotten Lian Po and Lin Xiangru, Kou Xun and Jia Fu?

sentences.zh: 吾本以濟國活家，豈計此之升降。

translations.literal: I originally meant to save the state and preserve the household — how could I calculate such rise and fall."
translations.idiomatic: I originally meant to save the state and preserve the household — how could I calculate such rise and fall?"

sentences.zh: 」明旦進戰，自寅訖午，大破賊於赭圻。

translations.literal: The next morning they advanced to battle; from the hour of Yin to the hour of Wu they crushed the rebels at Zhuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning they advanced to battle. From the hour of Yin to the hour of Wu they crushed the rebels at Zhuzhi.

sentences.zh: 尋進號輔國將軍，代孝祖督前鋒諸軍事。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to General Who Assists the State and replaced Xiaozu as commander of vanguard affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to General Who Assists the State and replaced Xiaozu as commander of vanguard affairs.

sentences.zh: 薛常保等在赭圻食盡，南賊大帥劉胡屯濃湖，以囊盛米系流查及船腹，陽覆船，順風流下，以餉赭圻。

translations.literal: Xue Changbao and others at Zhuzhi ran out of food; the great southern rebel commander Liu Hu was encamped at Nong Lake, tying bags of rice to floating logs and ship bellies, capsizing boats to drift them downwind to supply Zhuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Changbao and others at Zhuzhi ran out of food. The great southern rebel commander Liu Hu was encamped at Nong Lake, tying bags of rice to floating logs and ship bellies, capsizing boats to drift them downwind to supply Zhuzhi.

sentences.zh: 攸之疑其有異，遣人取船及流查，大得囊米，尋克赭圻。

translations.literal: Youzhi suspected something odd, sent men to take the boats and floating logs, obtained great quantities of bagged rice, and soon took Zhuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi then suspected something odd, sent men to take the boats and floating logs, obtained great quantities of bagged rice, and soon took Zhuzhi.

sentences.zh: 遷甯蠻校尉、雍州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commandant Who Pacifies the Tribes, Inspector of Yong Province, with grand command.
translations.idiomatic: He became transferred to Commandant Who Pacifies the Tribes, Inspector of Yong Province, with grand command.

sentences.zh: 袁顗復率大眾來入鵲尾，相持既久，軍主張興世越鵲尾上據錢溪，劉胡自攻之。

translations.literal: Yuan Yan again led a great host into Quewei; after long stalemate army commander Zhang Xingshi crossed above Quewei and held Qianxi; Liu Hu came himself to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yan again led a great host into Quewei. After a long stalemate army commander Zhang Xingshi crossed above Quewei and held Qianxi. Liu Hu came himself to attack.

sentences.zh: 攸之率諸將攻濃湖。

translations.literal: Youzhi led the generals to attack Nong Lake.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi then led the generals to attack Nong Lake.

sentences.zh: 錢溪信至大破賊，攸之悉以錢溪所送胡軍耳鼻示之。

translations.literal: When word came from Qianxi of great victory over the rebels Youzhi displayed to them all the ears and noses of Hu's troops sent from Qianxi.
translations.idiomatic: When word came from Qianxi of great victory over the rebels Youzhi displayed to them all the ears and noses of Hu's troops sent from Qianxi.

sentences.zh: 顗駭懼，急追胡還。

translations.literal: Yan was terrified and urgently recalled Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was terrified and urgently recalled Hu.

sentences.zh: 攸之諸軍悉力進攻，多所斬獲，胡於是棄眾而奔，顗亦奔走。

translations.literal: Youzhi's armies pressed the attack with all strength, killing and capturing many; Hu then abandoned his host and fled, and Yan also fled.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi's armies pressed the attack with all strength, killing and capturing many. Hu then abandoned his host and fled, and Yan also fled.

sentences.zh: 赭圻、濃湖之平也，賊軍委棄資財，珍貨山積，諸軍各競收斂，唯攸之、張興世約勒所部，不犯毫芥，諸將以此多之。

translations.literal: At the pacification of Zhuzhi and Nong Lake the rebel armies abandoned wealth and precious goods piled like mountains; each army competed to gather them, but only Youzhi and Zhang Xingshi restrained their troops from touching the slightest thing — the generals therefore praised them.
translations.idiomatic: At the pacification of Zhuzhi and Nong Lake the rebel armies abandoned wealth and precious goods piled like mountains. Each army competed to gather them, but only Youzhi and Zhang Xingshi restrained their troops from touching the slightest thing — the generals therefore praised them.

sentences.zh: 攸之進平尋陽，遷中領軍，封貞陽縣公。

translations.literal: Youzhi advanced to pacify Xunyang and was transferred to Central Palace Attendant, enfeoffed Duke of Zhenyang county.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi then advanced to pacify Xunyang and was transferred to Central Palace Attendant, enfeoffed Duke of Zhenyang county.

sentences.zh: 時劉遵考為光祿大夫，攸之在御坐謂遵考曰：「形陋之人今何如？

translations.literal: At the time Liu Zunkao was Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; Youzhi in the imperial presence said to Zunkao: "How is the ugly man now?"
translations.idiomatic: At the time Liu Zunkao was Grand Master of Splendid Happiness. Youzhi in the imperial presence said to Zunkao, "How is the ugly man now?"

sentences.zh: 」帝問之，攸之依實對，帝大笑。

translations.literal: The emperor asked; Youzhi answered truthfully and the emperor laughed heartily.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then asked; Youzhi answered truthfully and the emperor laughed heartily.

sentences.zh: 累遷郢州刺史，為政刻暴，或鞭士大夫。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Inspector of Ying Province; his governance was harsh and cruel, sometimes flogging scholar-officials.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Inspector of Ying Province. His governance was harsh and cruel, sometimes flogging scholar-officials.

sentences.zh: 上佐以下有忤意，輒面加詈辱。

translations.literal: Subordinates who displeased him he would face and revile.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates who displeased him he would face and revile.

sentences.zh: 而曉達吏事，自強不息，士庶畏憚，人莫敢欺。

translations.literal: Yet he understood administrative affairs and strove without ceasing; gentry and commoners feared him and none dared deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he understood administrative affairs and strove without ceasing. Gentry and commoners feared him and none dared deceive him.

sentences.zh: 聞有猛獸，輒自圍捕，往無不得，一日或得兩三。

translations.literal: Hearing of fierce beasts he would personally surround and capture them; he never failed, sometimes taking two or three in a day.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of fierce beasts he would personally surround and capture them. He never failed, sometimes taking two or three in a day.

sentences.zh: 若逼暮不禽，則宿昔圍守。

translations.literal: If by evening he had not taken one he would camp overnight in siege.
translations.idiomatic: If by evening he had not taken one he would camp overnight in siege.

sentences.zh: 賦斂嚴苦，徵發無度，繕修船舸，營造器甲。

translations.literal: Taxes were harsh and levies endless; he repaired ships and forged armor.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes were harsh and levies endless. He repaired ships and forged armor.

sentences.zh: 自至夏口，便有異圖。

translations.literal: From the time he reached Xiakou he already harbored other designs.
translations.idiomatic: From the time he reached Xiakou he already harbored other designs.

sentences.zh: 進監豫、司之二郡軍事，進號鎮軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to supervise military affairs of Yu and Si provinces and promoted to General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: He became promoted to supervise military affairs of Yu and Si provinces and promoted to General Who Pacifies the Army.

sentences.zh: 江州刺史桂陽王休範密有異志，欲以微旨動攸之，使道士陳公昭作天公書一函，題言沈丞相，送攸之門者。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jiang Province Prince Xiufan of Guiyang secretly harbored other designs and wished to move Youzhi with subtle hints; he had a Daoist Chen Gongzhao make a letter from the Heavenly Lord in one case addressed to Chancellor Shen and sent it to Youzhi's gate.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector of Jiang Province Prince Xiufan of Guiyang secretly harbored other designs and wished to move Youzhi with subtle hints. He had a Daoist Chen Gongzhao make a letter from the Heavenly Lord in one case addressed to Chancellor Shen and sent it to Youzhi's gate.

sentences.zh: 攸之不開書，推撿得公昭，送之朝廷。

translations.literal: Youzhi did not open the letter but traced and seized Gongzhao and sent him to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi then did not open the letter but traced and seized Gongzhao and sent him to the court.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝元徽二年，休範舉兵襲都，攸之謂僚佐曰：「桂陽今逼朝廷，必聲言吾與之同，若不顛沛勤王，必增朝野之惑。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanhui of the Deposed Emperor Xiufan raised troops and struck the capital; Youzhi told his staff: "Guiyang now presses the court and will surely claim I am with him — if I do not rush to aid the throne in crisis it will only increase court and common confusion.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanhui of the Deposed Emperor Xiufan raised troops and struck the capital. Youzhi told his staff, "Guiyang now presses the court and will surely claim I am with him — if I do not rush to aid the throne in crisis it will only increase court and common confusion.

sentences.zh: 」於是遣使受郢州刺史晉熙王燮節度。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent envoys to accept the command of Inspector of Ying Province Prince Xie of Jinxi.
translations.idiomatic: At that point he sent envoys to accept the command of Inspector of Ying Province Prince Xie of Jinxi.

sentences.zh: 會休范平，使乃還。

translations.literal: When Xiufan was pacified the envoys returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiufan was pacified the envoys returned.

sentences.zh: 進號征西大將軍、開府儀同三司，固讓開府。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Grand General of the Western Campaign, privilege equal to the Three Dukes, firmly declining the privilege.
translations.idiomatic: He became promoted to Grand General of the Western Campaign, privilege equal to the Three Dukes, firmly declining the privilege.

sentences.zh: 攸之自擅閫外，朝廷疑憚之，累欲征入，慮不受命，乃止。

translations.literal: Youzhi acted on his own authority beyond the gate; the court suspected and feared him and repeatedly wished to summon him in, fearing he would not obey and therefore stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi acted on his own authority beyond the gate. The court suspected and feared him and repeatedly wished to summon him in, fearing he would not obey and therefore stopped.

sentences.zh: 四年，建平王景素據京城反，攸之復應朝廷，景素尋平。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Prince Jingsu of Jianping rebelled holding the capital; Youzhi again responded to the court and Jingsu was soon pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Prince Jingsu of Jianping rebelled holding the capital. Youzhi again responded to the court and Jingsu was soon pacified.

sentences.zh: 時有台直合高道慶家在江陵，攸之初至州，道慶在家，牒其親戚十餘人，求州從事西曹，攸之為用三人。

translations.literal: At the time Palace Attendant Gao Daoqing's family was in Jiangling; when Youzhi first arrived at the province Daoqing was at home and petitioned for more than ten kinsmen as Western Bureau staff; Youzhi employed three.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Palace Attendant Gao Daoqing's family was in Jiangling. When Youzhi first arrived at the province Daoqing was at home and petitioned for more than ten kinsmen as Western Bureau staff. Youzhi employed three.

sentences.zh: 道慶大怒，自入州取教毀之而去。

translations.literal: Daoqing was furious, entered the province himself, took the commission and tore it up and left.
translations.idiomatic: Daoqing was furious, entered the province himself, took the commission and tore it up and left.

sentences.zh: 道慶素便馬，攸之與宴飲於聽事前，合馬槊，道慶槊中攸之馬鞍，攸之怒索刃槊，道慶馳馬而出。

translations.literal: Daoqing was skilled at horsemanship; Youzhi joined him in drinking before the audience hall and they matched with cavalry lances; Daoqing's lance struck Youzhi's saddle and Youzhi angrily demanded a blade-lance; Daoqing galloped out.
translations.idiomatic: Daoqing was skilled at horsemanship. Youzhi joined him in drinking before the audience hall and they matched with cavalry lances. Daoqing's lance struck Youzhi's saddle and Youzhi angrily demanded a blade-lance. Daoqing galloped out.

sentences.zh: 還都說攸之反狀，請三千人襲之。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital he reported Youzhi's rebellious conduct and requested three thousand men to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to the capital he reported Youzhi's rebellious conduct and requested three thousand men to attack him.

sentences.zh: 朝議慮其事難濟，高帝又保持不許。

translations.literal: Court deliberation feared the affair could not succeed; the High Emperor also restrained and did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Court deliberation feared the affair could not succeed; Emperor Gao also restrained and did not permit it.

sentences.zh: 楊運長等常相疑畏，乃與道慶密遣刺客齎廢帝手詔，以金餅賜攸之，州府佐吏進其階級。

translations.literal: Yang Yunchang and others constantly suspected and feared him; they secretly sent assassins with the Deposed Emperor's handwritten edict, granting Youzhi gold cakes and promoting his provincial staff in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yunchang and others constantly suspected and feared him. They secretly sent assassins with the Deposed Emperor's handwritten edict, granting Youzhi gold cakes and promoting his provincial staff in rank.

sentences.zh: 時有象三頭至江陵城北數里，攸之自出格殺之，忽有流矢集攸之馬鄣泥，其後刺客事發。

translations.literal: At the time three elephants came to several li north of Jiangling city; Youzhi went out himself and killed them; suddenly a stray arrow struck Youzhi's saddle mud-guard; afterward the assassin affair was exposed.
translations.idiomatic: At the time three elephants came to several li north of Jiangling city. Youzhi went out himself and killed them. Suddenly a stray arrow struck Youzhi's saddle mud-guard. Afterward the assassin affair was exposed.

sentences.zh: 廢帝既殞，順帝即位，加攸之車騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: After the Deposed Emperor died and Emperor Shun ascended, Youzhi was promoted to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, privilege equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: After the Deposed Emperor died and Emperor Shun ascended the throne, Youzhi was promoted to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, privilege equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝遣攸之子司徒左長史元琰齎廢帝刳斮之具以示之，攸之曰：「吾甯為王淩死，不作賈充生。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao of Qi sent Youzhi's son Left Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Works Yuan Yan bearing the Deposed Emperor's dismemberment implements to show him; Youzhi said: "I would rather die like Wang Ling than live like Jia Chong."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao of Qi sent Youzhi's son Left Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Works Yuan Yan bearing the Deposed Emperor's dismemberment implements to show him. Youzhi said, "I would rather die like Wang Ling than live like Jia Chong."

sentences.zh: 」尚未得即起兵，乃上表稱慶，並與齊高帝書推功。

translations.literal: Not yet able to rise immediately he memorialized congratulations and in a letter to Emperor Gao of Qi attributed merit to him.
translations.idiomatic: Not yet able to rise immediately he memorialized congratulations and in a letter to Emperor Gao of Qi attributed merit to him.

sentences.zh: 攸之有素書十數行，常韜在兩襠角，雲是宋明帝與己約誓。

translations.literal: Youzhi had a plain letter of ten-odd lines always hidden in the corners of his trousers, saying it was Emperor Ming of Song's covenant with him.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi then had a plain letter of ten-odd lines always hidden in the corners of his trousers, saying it was Emperor Ming of Song's covenant with him.

sentences.zh: 又皇太后使至，賜攸之燭十挺，割之得太后手令，曰：「國家之事，一以委公」。

translations.literal: Also an empress dowager envoy came granting Youzhi ten candles of wax; cutting them he obtained the empress dowager's handwritten order saying: "Affairs of state — all are entrusted to you."
translations.idiomatic: Also an empress dowager envoy came granting Youzhi ten candles of wax. Cutting them he obtained the empress dowager's handwritten order saying, "Affairs of state — all are entrusted to you."

sentences.zh: 明日，遂舉兵。

translations.literal: The next day he raised troops.
translations.idiomatic: The following day he rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 其妾崔氏、許氏諫曰：「官年已老，那不為百口作計。

translations.literal: His concubines Lady Cui and Lady Xu remonstrated: "You are already old — ought you not plan for your hundred mouths?"
translations.idiomatic: His concubines Lady Cui and Lady Xu remonstrated, "You are already old — ought you not plan for the lives of your household?"

sentences.zh: 」攸之指兩襠角示之。

translations.literal: Youzhi pointed to the corners of his trousers and showed them.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi pointed to the corners of his trousers and showed them the covenant.

sentences.zh: 攸之素畜士馬，資用豐積，至是戰士十萬，鐵馬三千。

translations.literal: Youzhi had long kept soldiers and horses and amassed abundant supplies; by now he had a hundred thousand warriors and three thousand armored horses.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi had long kept soldiers and horses and amassed abundant supplies. By now he had a hundred thousand warriors and three thousand armored horses.

sentences.zh: 將發江陵，使沙門釋僧粲筮之，云：「不至都，當自郢州回還。」

translations.literal: About to depart from Jiangling he had the monk Shi Sengcan divined, who said: "You will not reach the capital — you will turn back from Ying Province."
translations.idiomatic: About to depart from Jiangling he had the monk Shi Sengcan cast a divination, who said, "You will not reach the capital — you will turn back from Ying Province."

sentences.zh: 意甚不悅。

translations.literal: He was greatly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: He became greatly displeased.

sentences.zh: 初發江津，有氣狀如塵霧從西北來，正蓋軍上。

translations.literal: When first setting out from Jiangjin there was a vapor like dust and mist coming from the northwest, covering the army directly overhead.
translations.idiomatic: When first setting out from Jiangjin a vapor like dust and mist came from the northwest, covering the army directly overhead.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝遣眾軍西討，攸之盡銳攻郢州，行事柳世隆屢破之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao of Qi sent armies west to attack; Youzhi brought his full strength against Ying Province and was repeatedly defeated by Acting Administrator Liu Shilong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao of Qi sent armies west to attack. Youzhi brought his full strength against Ying Province and was repeatedly defeated by Acting Administrator Liu Shilong.

sentences.zh: 升明二年，還向江陵，未至，城已為雍州刺史張敬兒所據，無所歸，乃與第三子中書侍郎文和至華容之賞頭林，投州吏家。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengming he turned back toward Jiangling; before he arrived the city had already been taken by Inspector of Yong Province Zhang Jinger and he had nowhere to go. He went with his third son Secretariat Gentleman Wenhe to Shangtou Forest in Huarong and sought refuge in a district clerk's home.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shengming he turned back toward Jiangling. Before he arrived the city had already been taken by Inspector of Yong Province Zhang Jinger and he had nowhere to go. He went with his third son, Secretariat Gentleman Wenhe, to Shangtou Forest in Huarong and sought refuge in a district clerk's home.

sentences.zh: 此吏嘗為攸之所鞭，待攸之甚厚，不以往罰為怨，殺豚薦食。

translations.literal: This clerk had once been flogged by Youzhi yet treated Youzhi very generously, not resenting the past punishment, and slaughtered a pig to offer food.
translations.idiomatic: This clerk had once been flogged by Youzhi yet treated him very generously, not resenting the past punishment, and slaughtered a pig to offer food.

sentences.zh: 既而村人欲取之，攸之于櫟林與文和俱自經死，村人斬首送之都。

translations.literal: Before long the villagers wished to seize him; Youzhi and Wenhe both hanged themselves in the oak grove, and the villagers cut off their heads and sent them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the villagers wished to seize him. Youzhi and Wenhe both hanged themselves in the oak grove, and the villagers cut off their heads and sent them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 或割其腹，心有五竅。

translations.literal: Some cut open his belly and found his heart had five openings.
translations.idiomatic: Some cut open his belly and found his heart had five openings.

sentences.zh: 征西主簿苟昭先以家財葬攸之。

translations.literal: Western Campaigning Chief Clerk Gou Zhaoxian buried Youzhi at his own family's expense.
translations.idiomatic: Western Campaigning Chief Clerk Gou Zhaoxian buried Youzhi at his own family's expense.

sentences.zh: 攸之晚好讀書，手不釋卷，史、漢事多所記憶。

translations.literal: In his later years Youzhi loved reading and never put books down; he remembered much from the Records and the History.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Youzhi loved reading and never put books down. He remembered much from the Records and the History.

sentences.zh: 常歎曰：「早知窮達有命，恨不十年讀書。

translations.literal: He often sighed: "Had I known early that success and failure have fate, I regret not having read books for ten years."
translations.idiomatic: He often sighed, "Had I known early that success and failure have fate, I would regret not having read books for ten years."

sentences.zh: 」及攻郢城，夜嘗風浪，米船沈沒。

translations.literal: When attacking Ying city one night there were wind and waves and the rice boats sank.
translations.idiomatic: When attacking Ying city one night there were wind and waves and the rice boats sank.

sentences.zh: 倉曹參軍崔靈鳳女先適柳世隆子，攸之正色謂曰：「當今軍糧要急，而卿不以在意，由與城內婚姻邪。

translations.literal: Granary Adjutant Cui Lingfeng's daughter had earlier married Liu Shilong's son; Youzhi said sternly: "Military grain is urgent now — yet you pay it no mind. Is it because of marriage ties inside the city?"
translations.idiomatic: Granary Adjutant Cui Lingfeng's daughter had earlier married Liu Shilong's son. Youzhi said sternly, "Military grain is urgent now — yet you pay it no mind. Is it because of marriage ties inside the city?"

sentences.zh: 」靈鳳答曰：「樂廣有言，下官豈以五男易一女。

translations.literal: Lingfeng answered: "As Yue Guang said — would your humble servant trade five sons for one daughter?"
translations.idiomatic: Lingfeng answered, "As Yue Guang said — would your humble servant trade five sons for one daughter?"

sentences.zh: 」攸之歡然意解。

translations.literal: Youzhi was pleased and his anger dissolved.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi then was pleased and his anger dissolved.

sentences.zh: 攸之招集才力之士，隨郡人雙泰真有幹力，召不肯來。

translations.literal: Youzhi gathered men of talent and strength; Shuang Taizhen of Sui Commandery had ability but when summoned would not come.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi gathered men of talent and strength. Shuang Taizhen of Sui Commandery had ability but when summoned would not come.

sentences.zh: 攸之遣二十人被甲追之，泰真射殺數人，欲過家將母去，事迫不獲，單身走入蠻。

translations.literal: Youzhi sent twenty men in armor to pursue him; Taizhen shot and killed several, wished to pass home to take his mother but urgency prevented it and he fled alone into the tribal lands.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi sent twenty men in armor to pursue him. Taizhen shot and killed several, wished to pass home to take his mother but urgency prevented it, and he fled alone into the tribal lands.

sentences.zh: 追者既失之，錄其母去。

translations.literal: The pursuers having lost him took his mother away.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuers, having lost him, took his mother away.

sentences.zh: 泰真既失母，乃自歸，攸之不罪，曰：「此孝子也。

translations.literal: Taizhen having lost his mother then returned of himself; Youzhi did not punish him and said: "This is a filial son."
translations.idiomatic: Taizhen, having lost his mother, then returned of himself. Youzhi did not punish him and said, "This is a filial son."

sentences.zh: 」賜錢一萬，轉補隊主，其抑情待士如此。

translations.literal: He granted ten thousand cash and transferred him to squad leader — such was his restraint in treating men of worth.
translations.idiomatic: He granted ten thousand cash and transferred him to squad leader, such was his restraint in treating men of worth.

sentences.zh: 初，攸之賤時，與吳郡孫超之、全景文共乘一小船出都，三人共上引埭，有一人止而相之，曰：「君三人皆當至方伯。

translations.literal: Initially when Youzhi was lowly he shared a small boat leaving the capital with Sun Chaozhi of Wu Commandery and Quan Jingwen; the three together went up the Yin Embankment and a man stopped at the embankment and read their faces, saying: "You three will all reach regional lord rank."
translations.idiomatic: Initially when Youzhi was lowly he shared a small boat leaving the capital with Sun Chaozhi of Wu Commandery and Quan Jingwen. The three together went up the Yin Embankment and a man stopped and read their faces, saying, "You three will all reach regional lord rank."

sentences.zh: 」攸之曰：「豈有是事。

translations.literal: Youzhi said: "How could such a thing be."
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi said, "How could such a thing be?"

sentences.zh: 」相者曰：「不驗，便是相書誤耳。

translations.literal: The face-reader said: "If it is not verified, then my book of physiognomy is wrong."
translations.idiomatic: The face-reader said, "If it is not verified, then my book of physiognomy is wrong."

sentences.zh: 」後攸之為郢、荊二州，超之廣州刺史，景文南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Later Youzhi held Ying and Jing provinces, Chaozhi was Inspector of Guang Province, and Jingwen Inspector of Southern Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Later Youzhi held Ying and Jing provinces, Chaozhi became Inspector of Guang Province, and Jingwen Inspector of Southern Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 景文字弘達，齊永明中，卒于光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Jingwen styled Hongda; under Qi Yongming he died as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen, styled Hongda, died under Qi Yongming as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 攸之初至郢州，有順流之志，府主簿宗儼之勸攻郢城。

translations.literal: When Youzhi first reached Ying Province he had the mind to go downstream; headquarters Chief Clerk Zong Yanzhi urged attacking Ying city.
translations.idiomatic: When Youzhi first reached Ying Province he had the mind to go downstream. Headquarters Chief Clerk Zong Yanzhi urged attacking Ying city.

sentences.zh: 功曹臧寅以為攻守勢異，非旬日所拔，若不時舉，挫銳損威，攸之不從。

translations.literal: Merits Officer Zang Yin thought attack and defense positions differed and it could not be taken in ten days; if not raised in time, sharpness would be blunted and prestige damaged — Youzhi did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Merits Officer Zang Yin thought attack and defense positions differed and the city could not be taken in ten days. If not raised in time, sharpness would be blunted and prestige damaged — Youzhi did not listen.

sentences.zh: 既敗，諸將帥皆奔散，或呼寅俱亡。

translations.literal: Once defeated the generals all fled and scattered; some called Yin to flee with them.
translations.idiomatic: Once defeated the generals all fled and scattered. Some called Yin to flee with them.

sentences.zh: 寅曰：「我委質事人，豈可幸其成而責其敗。

translations.literal: Yin said: "I have entrusted my person to serve another — how can I rejoice in his success yet blame his failure."
translations.idiomatic: Yin said, "I have entrusted my person to serve another — how can I rejoice in his success yet blame his failure?"

sentences.zh: 」乃投水死。

translations.literal: Thereupon he threw himself into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: At that point he threw himself into the water and died.

sentences.zh: 又倉曹參軍金城邊榮為府錄事所辱，攸之為榮鞭殺錄事。

translations.literal: Also Granary Adjutant Bian Rong of Jincheng was insulted by the headquarters recorder; Youzhi flogged and killed the recorder for Rong's sake.
translations.idiomatic: Also Granary Adjutant Bian Rong of Jincheng was insulted by the headquarters recorder. Youzhi flogged and killed the recorder for Rong's sake.

sentences.zh: 攸之自江陵下，以榮為留府司馬守城。

translations.literal: When Youzhi went downstream from Jiangling he made Rong headquarters major to hold the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Youzhi went downstream from Jiangling he made Rong headquarters major to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 張敬兒將至，人或說之使詣敬兒降。

translations.literal: When Zhang Jinger was about to arrive some urged Rong to go to Jinger and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jinger was about to arrive some urged Rong to go to Jinger and surrender.

sentences.zh: 榮曰：「受沈公厚恩，一朝緩急，便改易本心，不能也。

translations.literal: Rong said: "I received great favor from Master Shen — at a moment of urgency to change my heart I cannot."
translations.idiomatic: Rong said, "I received great favor from Master Shen — at a moment of urgency to change my heart I cannot."

sentences.zh: 」城敗見敬兒，敬兒問曰：「邊公何為同人作賊，不早來。

translations.literal: When the city fell he saw Jinger; Jinger asked: "Why did Lord Bian join others as a rebel and not come earlier."
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he saw Jinger. Jinger asked, "Why did Lord Bian join others as a rebel and not come earlier?"

sentences.zh: 」榮曰：「沈荊州舉義兵，匡社稷，身雖可滅，要是宋世忠臣。

translations.literal: Rong said: "Inspector Shen of Jing raised righteous troops to restore the altars of state; though his person may be destroyed, he was nonetheless a loyal minister of the Song."
translations.idiomatic: Rong said, "Inspector Shen of Jing raised righteous troops to restore the altars of state. Though his person may be destroyed, he was nonetheless a loyal minister of the Song."

sentences.zh: 天下尚有直言之士，不可謂之為賊。

translations.literal: The realm still has men who speak straight — he cannot be called a rebel.
translations.idiomatic: The realm still has men who speak straight, he cannot be called a rebel.

sentences.zh: 身本不蘄生，何須見問。

translations.literal: I originally did not seek life — why need you ask."
translations.idiomatic: I originally did not seek life — why need you ask?"

sentences.zh: 」敬兒曰：「死何難。

translations.literal: Jinger said: "Death is not hard."
translations.idiomatic: Jinger said, "Death is not hard."

sentences.zh: 」命斬之，榮歡笑而去，容無異色。

translations.literal: He ordered execution; Rong went smiling, his bearing unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered execution. Rong went smiling, his bearing unchanged.

sentences.zh: 泰山程邕之者，素依隨榮，至是抱持榮謂敬兒曰：「君入人國，不聞仁惠之聲，而先戮義士，三楚之人，甯蹈江、漢而死，豈肯與將軍同日以生。

translations.literal: Cheng Yongzhi of Mount Tai had long relied on Rong; now he embraced Rong and told Jinger: "You enter another's state and before we hear the sound of benevolence you first execute a man of righteousness — the people of the Three Chu regions would rather throw themselves into the Yangtze and Han and die than live one day with the general."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yongzhi of Mount Tai had long relied on Rong. Now he embraced Rong and told Jinger, "You enter another's state and before we hear the sound of benevolence you first execute a man of righteousness — the people of the Three Chu regions would rather throw themselves into the Yangtze and Han and die than live one day with the general."

sentences.zh: 」敬兒曰：「求死甚易，何為不許。

translations.literal: Jinger said: "Seeking death is very easy — why not permit it."
translations.idiomatic: Jinger said, "Seeking death is very easy — why not permit it?"

sentences.zh: 」先殺邕之然後及榮，三軍莫不垂泣，曰：「奈何一日殺二義士。

translations.literal: He first killed Yongzhi and then Rong; the whole army wept and said: "How can one day kill two men of righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: He first killed Yongzhi and then Rong. The whole army wept and said, "How can one day kill two men of righteousness?"

sentences.zh: 」比之臧洪及陳容。

translations.literal: They were compared to Zang Hong and Chen Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Later generations compared them to Zang Hong and Chen Rong.

sentences.zh: 廢帝之殞，攸之欲起兵，問知星人葛珂之。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor died Youzhi wished to raise troops and asked the star-knowing man Ge Kezhi.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor died Youzhi wished to raise troops and asked the star-knowing man Ge Kezhi.

sentences.zh: 珂之曰：「起兵皆候太白，太白見則成，伏則敗。

translations.literal: Kezhi said: "Raising troops all depend on the Great White Star — when the Great White appears it succeeds, when it hides it fails."
translations.idiomatic: Kezhi said, "Raising troops all depend on the Great White Star — when the Great White appears it succeeds, when it hides it fails."

sentences.zh: 昔桂陽乙太白伏時舉兵，一戰授首，此近世明驗。

translations.literal: In old times when Guiyang rose at the time the Great White was hidden, one battle and he lost his head — this is a clear recent verification."
translations.idiomatic: In old times when Guiyang rose at the time the Great White was hidden, one battle and he lost his head, this is a clear recent verification."

sentences.zh: 今蕭公廢昏立明，正逢太白伏時，此與天合也。

translations.literal: Now Lord Xiao deposed the wicked and established the enlightened, exactly when the Great White is hidden — this accords with Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Now Lord Xiao deposed the wicked and established the enlightened, exactly when the Great White is hidden, this accords with Heaven."

sentences.zh: 且太白尋出東方利用兵，西方不利。

translations.literal: Moreover the Great White will soon emerge in the east where troops are favorable; the west is unfavorable."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Great White will soon emerge in the east where troops are favorable. the west is unfavorable."

sentences.zh: 」故攸之止不下。

translations.literal: Therefore Youzhi stopped and did not go downstream.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Youzhi stopped and did not go downstream.

sentences.zh: 及後舉兵，珂之又曰：「今歲星守南斗，其國不可伐。

translations.literal: When later he raised troops Kezhi again said: "This year the Year Star guards the Southern Dipper — that state cannot be attacked."
translations.idiomatic: When later he raised troops Kezhi again said, "This year the Year Star guards the Southern Dipper — that state cannot be attacked."

sentences.zh: 」攸之不從，果敗。

translations.literal: Youzhi did not listen and indeed was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi then did not listen and indeed was defeated.

sentences.zh: 攸之表檄文疏，皆其記室南陽宗儼之辭也，事敗責之，答曰：「士為知己，豈為君輩所識。

translations.literal: Youzhi's memorials, proclamations and documents were all the words of his secretary Zong Yanzhi of Nanyang; when the affair failed Youzhi blamed him and he answered: "A gentleman serves a knowing master — how could he be known by the likes of you."
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi's memorials, proclamations, and documents were all the words of his secretary Zong Yanzhi of Nanyang. When the affair failed Youzhi blamed him and he answered, "A gentleman serves a knowing master — how could he be known by the likes of you?"

sentences.zh: 」遂伏誅。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: At that point he was executed.

sentences.zh: 攸之景和中與齊高帝同直殿省，申以歡好，帝以長女義興憲公主妻攸之第三子文和，生二女，並養之宮中，恩禮甚厚，及嫁皆得素舊，公家營遣焉。

translations.literal: In Jinghe Youzhi and Emperor Gao of Qi shared duty in the palace hall and deepened their friendship; the emperor married his eldest daughter Princess Xian of Yixing to Youzhi's third son Wenhe. Two daughters were born and both were raised in the palace with great favor; when they married they all received old ties and the public household provided their dowries.
translations.idiomatic: In Jinghe Youzhi and Emperor Gao of Qi shared duty in the palace hall and deepened their friendship. The emperor married his eldest daughter Princess Xian of Yixing to Youzhi's third son Wenhe. Two daughters were born and both were raised in the palace with great favor. When they married they all received old ties and the public household provided their dowries.

sentences.zh: 齊武帝制以攸之弟雍之孫僧昭為義興公主後。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Qi decreed that Youzhi's younger brother Yongzhi's grandson Sengzhao be made heir to Princess Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Qi decreed that Youzhi's younger brother Yongzhi's grandson Sengzhao be made heir to Princess Yixing.

sentences.zh: 僧昭別名法朗，少事天師道士，常以甲子及甲午日，夜著黃巾衣褐醮於私室。

translations.literal: Sengzhao, alias Falang, in youth served Celestial Master Daoist priests and on the days jiazi and jiawu at night wore yellow headcloth and brown robes to perform rites in his private chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhao, alias Falang, in youth served Celestial Master Daoist priests. On the days jiazi and jiawu at night he wore yellow headcloth and brown robes to perform rites in his private chamber.

sentences.zh: 時記人吉凶，頗有應驗。

translations.literal: At the time he recorded men's fortunes and misfortunes and often had verified results.
translations.idiomatic: At the time he recorded men's fortunes and misfortunes and often had verified results.

sentences.zh: 自雲為泰山錄事，幽司中有所收錄，必僧昭署名。

translations.literal: He claimed himself to be a Mount Tai clerk; in the dark bureau whatever was recorded he must sign Sengzhao's name.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed himself to be a Mount Tai clerk. In the dark bureau whatever was recorded he must sign Sengzhao's name.

sentences.zh: 中年為山陰縣。

translations.literal: In middle age he served as magistrate of Shanyin county.
translations.idiomatic: In middle age he served as magistrate of Shanyin county.

sentences.zh: 梁武陵王紀為會稽太守，宴坐池亭，蛙鳴聒耳。

translations.literal: Prince Ji of Wuling of Liang was Administrator of Kuaiji and sat feasting in a pool pavilion; frogs croaked loudly in the ear.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ji of Wuling of Liang was Administrator of Kuaiji and sat feasting in a pool pavilion. Frogs croaked loudly in the ear.

sentences.zh: 王曰：「殊廢絲竹之聽。

translations.literal: The prince said: "This truly wastes the listening for silk and bamboo."
translations.idiomatic: The prince said, "This truly wastes the listening for silk and bamboo."

sentences.zh: 」僧昭咒厭十許口便息。

translations.literal: Sengzhao chanted a curse and after ten-odd breaths they ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhao chanted a curse and after ten-odd breaths they ceased.

sentences.zh: 及日晚，王又曰：「欲其復鳴。

translations.literal: When evening came the prince again said: "I wish them to croak again."
translations.idiomatic: When evening came the prince again said, "I wish them to croak again."

sentences.zh: 」僧昭曰：「王歡已闌，今恣汝鳴。

translations.literal: Sengzhao said: "Your Highness's pleasure is ended — now let you croak freely."
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhao said, "Your Highness's pleasure is ended — now let you croak freely."

sentences.zh: 」即便喧聒。

translations.literal: At once they clamored again.
translations.idiomatic: At once they clamored again.

sentences.zh: 又嘗校獵，中道而還，左右問其故，答曰：「國家有邊事，須還處分。

translations.literal: Also once on a hunt he turned back midway; attendants asked the reason and he answered: "The state has frontier affairs and I must return to handle them."
translations.idiomatic: Also once on a hunt he turned back midway. Attendants asked the reason and he answered, "The state has frontier affairs and I must return to handle them."

sentences.zh: 」問何以知之，曰：「向聞南山虎嘯知耳。

translations.literal: Asked how he knew he said: "Just now hearing the southern mountain tiger roar I knew."
translations.idiomatic: Asked how he knew he said, "Just now hearing the southern mountain tiger roar I knew."

sentences.zh: 」俄而使至。

translations.literal: Before long a messenger arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Before long a messenger arrived.

sentences.zh: 復謂人曰：「吾昔為幽司所使，實為煩碎，今已自解。

translations.literal: Again he told people: "I was formerly made envoy by the dark bureau and it was truly tedious; now I have released myself."
translations.idiomatic: Again he told people, "I was formerly made envoy by the dark bureau and it was truly tedious. Now I have released myself."

sentences.zh: 」乃開匣出黃紙書，上有一大字，字不可識。

translations.literal: Thereupon he opened a box and took out yellow paper with writing; on it was one large character that could not be recognized.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he opened a box and took out yellow paper with writing. On it was one large character that could not be recognized.

sentences.zh: 曰：「教分判如此。」

translations.literal: He said: "The instruction was to divide judgment thus."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "The instruction was to divide judgment thus."

sentences.zh: 及太清初，謂親知曰：「明年海內喪亂，生靈十不一存。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichu he told close acquaintances: "Next year within the seas there will be chaos and disorder; of the living not one in ten will remain."
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taichu he told close acquaintances, "Next year within the seas there will be chaos and disorder. Of the living not one in ten will remain."

sentences.zh: 」乃苦求東歸。

translations.literal: Thereupon he bitterly sought to return east.
translations.idiomatic: At that point he bitterly sought to return east.

sentences.zh: 既不獲許，及亂，百口皆殲。

translations.literal: When permission was not granted, when the turmoil came his hundred mouths were all exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Once permission was not granted, when the turmoil came his hundred mouths were all exterminated.

sentences.zh: 僧昭位廷尉卿，太清三年卒。

translations.literal: Sengzhao held the post of Minister of Justice and died in the third year of Taiqing.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhao held the post of Minister of Justice and died in the third year of Taiqing.

sentences.zh: 宗愨字元幹，南陽涅陽人也。

translations.literal: Zong Que, styled Yuangan, was a man of Nieyang in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Que, styled Yuangan, came from Nieyang in Nanyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 叔父少文高尚不仕，愨年少，問其所志，愨答曰：「願乘長風破萬里浪。

translations.literal: His uncle Shaowen was lofty and did not take office; when Que was young he asked his ambition and Que answered: "I wish to ride the long wind and break ten thousand li of waves."
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Shaowen was lofty and did not take office. When Que was young he asked his ambition and Que answered, "I wish to ride the long wind and break ten thousand li of waves."

sentences.zh: 」少文曰：「汝若不富貴，必破我門戶。

translations.literal: Shaowen said: "If you do not become rich and honored you will surely ruin my household."
translations.idiomatic: Shaowen said, "If you do not become rich and honored you will surely ruin my household."

sentences.zh: 」兄泌娶妻，始入門夜被劫，愨年十四，挺身與劫相拒，十餘人皆披散，不得入室。

translations.literal: When elder brother Mi married, on the first night of entering the gate they were robbed; Que at fourteen stepped forward and resisted the robbers — more than ten men were scattered and could not enter the room.
translations.idiomatic: When elder brother Mi married, on the first night of entering the gate they were robbed. Que at fourteen stepped forward and resisted the robbers — more than ten men were scattered and could not enter the room.

sentences.zh: 時天下無事，士人並以文義為業，少文既高尚，諸子群從皆愛好墳典，而愨任氣好武，故不為鄉曲所知。

translations.literal: At the time the realm was at peace and gentlemen all took literary studies as their profession; Shaowen being lofty, his sons and kinsmen all loved the classics, but Que relied on spirit and loved martial affairs — therefore he was not known in the village.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the realm was at peace and gentlemen all took literary studies as their profession. Shaowen being lofty, his sons and kinsmen all loved the classics, but Que relied on spirit and loved martial affairs — therefore he was not known in the village.

sentences.zh: 江夏王義恭為征北將軍、南兗州刺史，愨隨鎮廣陵。

translations.literal: Prince Yigong of Jiangxia was General Who Campaigns North and Inspector of Southern Yan Province; Que followed the garrison at Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yigong of Jiangxia was General Who Campaigns North and Inspector of Southern Yan Province. Que followed the garrison at Guangling.

sentences.zh: 時從兄綺為征北府主簿，與愨同住，綺妾與給吏牛泰私通，綺入直，而泰潛來就綺妾。

translations.literal: At the time cousin Qi was chief clerk of the Northern Campaigning headquarters and lived with Que; Qi's concubine had a private affair with the supply clerk Niu Tai; Qi entered duty and Tai secretly came to Qi's concubine.
translations.idiomatic: At the time cousin Qi was chief clerk of the Northern Campaigning headquarters and lived with Que. Qi's concubine had a private affair with the supply clerk Niu Tai. Qi entered duty and Tai secretly came to Qi's concubine.

sentences.zh: 愨知之，入殺牛泰然後白綺。

translations.literal: Que knew of it, entered and killed Tai then reported to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Que knew of it, entered and killed Tai, then reported to Qi.

sentences.zh: 義恭壯其意，不罪也。

translations.literal: Yigong admired his intent and did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong admired his spirit and did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 後以補國上軍將軍。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Supplementary General of the Upper Army of the State.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he was appointed Supplementary General of the Upper Army of the State.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十二年，伐林邑，愨自奮願行，義恭舉愨有膽勇，乃除振武將軍，為安西參軍蕭景憲軍副。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Yuanjia, campaigning against Lin Yi, Que volunteered eagerly; Yigong recommended Que for courage and appointed him General Who Rouses Might as deputy to Western Campaigning Adjutant Xiao Jingxian.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Yuanjia, campaigning against Lin Yi, Que volunteered eagerly. Yigong recommended Que for courage and appointed him General Who Rouses Might as deputy to Western Campaigning Adjutant Xiao Jingxian.

sentences.zh: 隨交州刺史檀和之圍區粟城。

translations.literal: He followed Inspector of Jiao Province Tan Hezhi in besieging Qu Su city.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Inspector of Jiao Province Tan Hezhi in besieging Qu Su city.

sentences.zh: 林邑遣將范毗沙達來救區粟，和之遣偏軍拒之，為賊所敗。

translations.literal: Lin Yi sent General Fan Pisha to rescue Qu Su; Hezhi sent a detached force to resist and was defeated by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Yi sent General Fan Pisha to rescue Qu Su. Hezhi sent a detached force to resist and was defeated by the enemy.

sentences.zh: 又遣愨，愨乃分軍為數道，偃旗潛進討破之，仍攻拔區粟，入象浦。

translations.literal: He again sent Que; Que divided the army into several routes, lowered banners and secretly advanced in attack and broke them, then assaulted and took Qu Su and entered Elephant Ford.
translations.idiomatic: He again sent Que. Que divided the army into several routes, lowered banners and secretly advanced in attack and broke them, then assaulted and took Qu Su and entered Elephant Ford.

sentences.zh: 林邑王范陽邁傾國來逆，以具裝被象，前後無際。

translations.literal: King Fanyang Mai of Lin Yi brought the whole state to oppose them, with armored elephants front and back without end.
translations.idiomatic: King Fanyang Mai of Lin Yi brought the whole state to oppose them, with armored elephants front and back without end.

sentences.zh: 愨以為外國有師子威服百獸，乃制其形與象相禦，象果驚奔，眾因此潰亂，遂克林邑。

translations.literal: Que thought foreign lands had lions that awe a hundred beasts; he made their form to oppose the elephants and the elephants indeed fled in panic; the host therefore collapsed in disorder and Lin Yi was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Que thought foreign lands had lions that awe a hundred beasts. He made their form to oppose the elephants and the elephants indeed fled in panic. The host therefore collapsed in disorder and Lin Yi was taken.

sentences.zh: 收其珍異，皆是未名之寶，其餘雜物不可稱計。

translations.literal: They collected rare treasures, all nameless gems; the rest of the miscellaneous goods cannot be counted.
translations.idiomatic: They collected rare treasures, all nameless gems. The rest of the miscellaneous goods cannot be counted.

sentences.zh: 愨一毫無犯，唯有被梳枕刷，此外蕭然。

translations.literal: Que took not the slightest for himself — only a quilt, comb, pillow and brush; beyond that he was bare.
translations.idiomatic: Que took not the slightest for himself — only a quilt, comb, pillow, and brush. Beyond that he was bare.

sentences.zh: 文帝甚嘉之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen greatly praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen praised this highly.

sentences.zh: 三十年，孝武伐逆，以愨為南中郎諮議參軍，領中兵。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, when Xiaowu punished the rebel, Que was made Advisory Adjutant of the Southern Central Office leading the middle army.
translations.idiomatic: During the thirtieth year, when Xiaowu punished the rebel, Que was made Advisory Adjutant of the Southern Central Office leading the middle army.

sentences.zh: 及事平，功次柳元景。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled his merit ranked next after Liu Yuanjing.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was settled his merit ranked second only to Liu Yuanjing.

sentences.zh: 大明三年，竟陵王誕據廣陵反，愨表求赴討，乘驛詣都，面受節度。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daming, Prince Dan of Jingling rebelled holding Guangling; Que memorialized requesting to go to suppress him, rode post relay to the capital and received command in person.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Daming, Prince Dan of Jingling rebelled holding Guangling. Que memorialized requesting to go suppress him, rode post relay to the capital, and received command in person.

sentences.zh: 上停輿慰勉，愨聳躍數十，左右顧眄，上壯之。

translations.literal: The emperor stopped his carriage to encourage him; Que leaped several times, looking left and right, and the emperor admired his vigor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stopped his carriage to encourage him. Que leaped several times, looking left and right, and the emperor admired his vigor.

sentences.zh: 及行，隸車騎大將軍沈慶之。

translations.literal: When he marched he served under Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry Shen Qingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: When he marched he served under Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry Shen Qingzhi.

sentences.zh: 初，誕誑其眾云：「宗愨助我。

translations.literal: Initially Dan deceived his host saying: "Zong Que assists me."
translations.idiomatic: Initially Dan deceived his troops, saying, "Zong Que assists me."

sentences.zh: 」及愨至，躍馬繞城呼曰：「我宗愨也。

translations.literal: When Que arrived he galloped around the walls calling: "I am Zong Que."
translations.idiomatic: When Que arrived he galloped around the walls calling, "I am Zong Que!"

sentences.zh: 」事平，入為左衛將軍。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he entered court as General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was settled he entered court as General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 五年，從獵墮馬腳折，不堪朝直，以為光祿大夫，加金章紫綬。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, following a hunt he fell from his horse and broke his leg, unable to attend court duty; he was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with golden seal and purple sash.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, following a hunt he fell from his horse and broke his leg and could no longer attend court duty. He was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with golden seal and purple sash.

sentences.zh: 有佳牛堪進禦，官買不肯賣，坐免官。

translations.literal: He had an excellent ox fit to present to the emperor; when officials came to buy it he would not sell and was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He had an excellent ox fit to present to the emperor. When officials came to buy it he would not sell and was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 明年復先職。

translations.literal: The next year he was restored to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was restored to his former post.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，為甯蠻校尉、雍州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor ascended he was made Commandant Who Pacifies the Tribes, Inspector of Yong Province, with grand command.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor ascended the throne he was made Commandant Who Pacifies the Tribes, Inspector of Yong Province, with grand command.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈征西將軍，諡曰肅侯，配食孝武廟庭。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously enfeoffed General of the Western Campaign with posthumous title Marquis Su, granted sacrifice in Emperor Xiaowu's temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously enfeoffed General of the Western Campaign with the posthumous title Marquis Su, granted sacrifice in Emperor Xiaowu's temple hall.

sentences.zh: 子羅雲，卒，子元寶嗣。

translations.literal: His son Luoyun died; son Yuanbao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Luoyun died; his son Yuanbao succeeded.

sentences.zh: 愨從子夬字明揚，祖少文，名列隱逸傳。

translations.literal: Que's cousin's son Guai styled Mingyang; grandfather Shaowen is listed in the Biographies of Recluses.
translations.idiomatic: Que's cousin's son Guai, styled Mingyang, had as grandfather Shaowen, who is listed in the Biographies of Recluses.

sentences.zh: 父繁，西中郎諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Father Fan was Advisory Adjutant of the Western Central Office.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fan served as Advisory Adjutant of the Western Central Office.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝起兵，遷西中郎諮議。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang raised troops Guai was transferred to Advisory Adjutant of the Western Central Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Liang raised troops Guai was transferred to Advisory Adjutant of the Western Central Office.

sentences.zh: 時西土位望，唯夬與同郡樂藹、劉坦為州人所推服，故領軍蕭穎胄深相委仗。

translations.literal: At the time among western gentry of rank and repute only Guai with Le Ai and Liu Tan of the same commandery were trusted by the people of the province; therefore Director of Palace Attendants Xiao Yingmao deeply entrusted them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time among western gentry of rank and repute only Guai, with Le Ai and Liu Tan of the same commandery, were trusted by the people of the province. Therefore Director of Palace Attendants Xiao Yingmao deeply entrusted them.

sentences.zh: 武帝受禪，曆太子右衛率，五兵尚書，參掌大選。

translations.literal: When the emperor received the abdication Guai successively held Right Guard of the Crown Prince, Minister of the Five Armies, and shared in grand selection.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor received the abdication Guai successively held Right Guard of the Crown Prince, Minister of the Five Armies, and shared in grand selection of officials.

sentences.zh: 天監三年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Tianjian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Tianjian.

sentences.zh: 子曜卿。

translations.literal: Son Yaoging.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yaoging.
